  • Access keys with their own role: keys could then hold more than their owner. Rejected (AUTH-07: keys only narrow).
  • The deny as a role (No access is a role with no permissions): a role adds, it cannot take away. Rejected.

Enforced by

ARCH-PERMS, ARCH-AUTHZ-ONLY, ARCH-API-OUT, ARCH-PERSON-REF, ARCH-NO-COUNTERS, ARCH-EVENTS, ARCH-SETTINGS, DATA-MARKS and SEC-MATRIX (see tools/checks/catalog.toml), backed by the named tests of WP-05, WP-08, WP-09, WP-11 and WP-12; the per-request cache by review.

ADR-0026: One theme file for everything about how the app looks

Status: Accepted · 2026-10-08 · replaces the styling part of ADR-0010 · updated in M6: a base file and one file of colors and its shadow per theme (decision M6-Q1) · updated in M8: themes of your own (M8-Q8 to Q11)

Context

Requirement (M2C): all UI theming lives in one theming file, the way a sister project keeps its complete look in one theme file. ADR-0010 made design/tokens.json the source of colors, fonts, sizes, radii and shadows, but let every component keep its own CSS Module. The audit of M2C (section D) found what that costs:

  • 55 CSS modules with 3,261 lines; values that have no token (font-weight: 700 57 times, line heights 38 times, about 50 1px solid borders, a z-index chosen per file, opacities, keyframes);
  • the same rule copied into many modules (the focus ring 22 times, the muted text, .stack, .row), the skip link twice, and forced-colors handling in ten components;
  • the theme list written in tokens.json and again in the settings registry in Rust, held together by a test (M2C-F64);
  • theme names and the data-look attribute written by hand in TypeScript and in the browser tests.

The sister project compiles its theme to CSS in the browser and injects it as a style element. Bugaboo cannot do that: the content security policy is style-src 'self' (SEC-11), so nothing may put a style on the page at run time.

Decision

  1. One file, design/theme.kdl (KDL, decision M2C-Q1). It holds everything: the themes, the choices that change token values, every token with its variants per mode, the contrast rules, the mixins, the keyframes and the rules of every component. Comments are allowed, and each token is one line. It replaces design/tokens.json. Only cargo xtask gen theme reads it (with the kdl crate, pinned like the sister project's); the server and the browser never parse KDL.

  2. Values are tokens, with their variants per mode on the line of the token. A token has a kind (color, font, size, number, duration, easing, shadow, weight, line-height, border-width, layer, opacity) and, besides its value:

    • <theme>= for each of the four themes (colors and shadows), with kind="light" or "dark" on the theme;
    • <theme>-more= for a device that asks for more contrast (prefers-contrast: more);
    • forced= while forced colors are on (forced-colors: active);
    • <choice>= while a choice of the person is on: compact spacing, larger-text, less-motion (which the device can switch on too).

    Every token of ADR-0010 keeps its value; the file adds font weight, line height, border width, layers (z-index), opacity, easing, the brightness of a pressed primary button, and forced colors as a mode. The focus ring is two tokens (ring-width, ring-offset) and one mixin (ring) that every rule uses.

  3. Rules are part rules that use tokens only. part "button[variant=primary]:hover" { background "$accent" } styles every element that says data-part="button" and data-variant="primary". A value is a word, 0, a percentage, or $token (written var(--token) in the output); a length, color, duration, weight, line height, layer or opacity written out is a finding of LINT-CSS and STY-TOKENS. base rules style the page frame (html, body); mixin, keyframes and forced { … }, more-contrast { … }, media "…" { … } blocks complete the language.

  4. Components carry no style values and no class names. They emit data-part, data-state and data-variant, through partOf(part.button, { variants: […], states: […] }) of @bugaboo/ui. The names of the parts and the words a part may have (partWords) are generated into tokens.ts from the rules, so a misspelled part or word is a type error. React Aria's own data-* state attributes (data-hovered, data-pressed, data-selected, data-focus-visible, data-entering, …) are allowed and used: a rule names them as button[hovered].

  5. The file is compiled at build time into one static style sheet, web/packages/ui/src/theme.css (committed, with a copy for the design pages at docs/design/theme.css). The content security policy stays style-src 'self'; no style element or attribute is made at run time. This is where Bugaboo differs from the sister project. Neither file is edited by hand: DOC-GENERATED compares them with the output of cargo xtask gen theme.

  6. The list of themes is written once. The four built-in themes (Daylight, Paper, Dusk, Midnight) and the two that start are defined in the file. gen theme writes them to TypeScript (tokens.ts: themeIds, lightThemeIds, darkThemeIds, the defaults) and to Rust (crates/bb-core/src/settings/themes.rs: the choices of the settings Light theme and Dark theme and their defaults, which catalog.rs names). The reader of the settings registry follows those names, so the browser's generated choices and defaults come from the same file. There is no hand-kept list in catalog.rs and no test that holds two lists together (closes M2C-F64).

  7. Custom themes, later, store token values only: names from the generated token list, values checked by the kind of the token. They never add a rule, a selector or CSS text. How the values reach the page without breaking the policy is decided when the theme editor is built.

  8. Contrast is checked per theme and per mode (STY-CONTRAST), the way the sister project's contrast check does: every text color on every background in each theme, and with <theme>-more= the 7:1 and 3:1 rules of ADR-0010. The rules for it are the contrast and distinct lines of the same file: hovered (the pair of a brightened main button as it is seen hovered), stronger (the quiet words of a row at 5:1 on the tints), lines (the edge of High, the hover line and the ring on the tints and surfaces) and fills (a fill that carries no text, the square of a label, held like a line at 3:1 on the surfaces, M5-F149) inside contrast; distinct also asks for a least difference of color (min-delta-e-…, CIE 1976 delta E) between the three status tints and the card, between the red of Critical and the orange of High, and between the squares of the twelve label colors, because a ratio only knows brightness. dimmed holds the page behind a sheet as it is drawn (the token scrim over the fill and the text of the page): the sheet stands out and the page text is dim. A distinct rule that names no minimum is a parse error. Bold is the same kind of rule: the file has one bold list that names the selectors that may set the bold weight, each with its role from UX §7.3 (STY-BOLD), so a bold that UX does not name cannot be added by accident.

  9. The design pages are generated too. docs/design/components.css, docpage.css, ux-design.css and mockup.css style the documents and mockups in docs/, not the app (the last two hold what the UX page and the mockup had in a <style> block, and the classes that replaced their style= attributes). They are written in the same file as docs blocks: rule lines with plain CSS selectors (the pages use class names and elements, which parts must not) that use tokens only, and the tokens of the pages themselves (doc-…), which go to docs/design/theme.css and not to the app's sheet. gen theme writes both sheets, LINT-CSS reads them like the parts, and DOC-GENERATED compares them (M2C-F93, done in C-06). The motion of the pages follows the motion tokens, so there is no reduced-motion rule with !important. THEME-ONLY reads the pages of docs/ too: no <style> element and no style attribute in the markup, unless the page's own script builds its value (a position or a color it computes, which is a style of the run time, M2C-F105).

  10. Moving was done in two steps. M2C C-01 built the engine and moved the primitives of packages/ui. M2C C-06 moved every app feature, the shell and the other components (M2C-F90): there is no CSS Module, no cx and no exemption any more, and THEME-ONLY passes with nothing exempt. What several features said the same way is one part (stack, text, muted, row, list, item, facts, hint, …, M2C-F65), and the focus ring, the skip link and the forced-colors outline of the marked item (marked) are written once.

  11. The names of the page frame are written once. The attributes of <html> that the sheets and the code use (data-look, data-theme, data-preview-look) are the frame line of the file. gen theme writes them to the sheets, to tokens.ts (pageAttributes), which theme.ts, the theme sample and the end-to-end specs read, and to docs/design/frame.js (bugabooFrame), which the scripts of the design pages read (M2C-F91). The choices (data-spacing, data-text, data-motion) are read from variants the same way.

Update (M3 WP-16, the new look)

  • Choices of the device. A variant may have only media= (no attribute on the page): touch ((pointer: coarse), (width < $bp-tablet)) gives a token its finger value (size-control 36 becomes 44, size-row 44 becomes 64), phone gives text 16. A media query may name a $token with a plain value.
  • Container queries. A rule may hold container "(min-width: $bp-window-side)" { … }, written as @container: a window follows its own width, not the screen's (UX §6.3).
  • Feature queries. A rule may hold supports "(width: calc(1px * (2px / 1px)))" { … }, written as @supports: a line that needs a newer browser is read only by a browser that has it, so the line before it stays where it does not. Variables inside a media block are no such guard: a browser that cannot compute them drops the line to its start value, not to the line before.
  • One run-time style. The size a person drags a window to is two variables of the theme file (window-width, window-height). The issue list adds four, for the same reason (a size the browser measures or the person drags, which no token can hold): list-columns, the widths of the columns that the head and every row share; list-gutter, the width of the scroll bar the rows have now, so the head keeps the same room and the columns stand over each other; and list-width, the width of the head as the browser measured it (as wide as its columns need), which is given to the virtualized rows because they have no width of their own, so head and rows scroll sideways as one; and size-code-char, one character of the code font as the browser draws it, measured from a probe in that font (the font of the computer may be any of its stack), so the ID column is as wide as the IDs really are. THEME-ONLY allows exactly element.style.setProperty(variableOf("…"), value): variableOf only takes the name of a token, and nothing else may set a style from code.
  • The pictures use the parts. cargo xtask gen theme also writes docs/design/parts.css, the rules of the parts without the tokens, so the pictures of the UX design are drawn with the same data-part markup as the app and cannot differ from it.
  • The icon of the app is drawn in the theme's colors (the favicon, M8). cargo xtask gen theme also writes web/app/public/favicon.svg and two PNG pictures of it (favicon-32.png, and apple-touch-icon.png for a page saved to a phone) in the accent and on-accent of the light theme that starts, so a new accent changes the icon too. The drawing is written once, in xtask/src/gen/favicon.rs; the PNG files are drawn from it on a fixed grid and encoded there, with no new dependency. DOC-GENERATED compares them byte for byte. Vite serves web/app/public at the root and the build copies it into the root of dist, which the server serves with the other files of the app. A web app manifest with larger icons belongs to the installable app (UX-03) and is not made yet.
  • Several distinct rules. The hovered and the selected row must differ from the tint of a status group as well as from the plain surfaces, so the file has one distinct rule for the plain surfaces and one for each tint.

Update (fonts like the sister project)

  • System font stacks, no font files. Decision: Bugaboo handles fonts like its sister project: the theme file has the sister project's four stacks word for word, and Bugaboo ships no font file, has no @font-face and asks no font service. The reasons: one look across the sister projects; nothing to download before the first page draws; no font licence to carry in the dependency register. A computer without the named faces takes its own system face (the last word of each stack), so text may look a little different between systems.
  • One token per role, the sister project's roles. font-ui is the text of the app (rows, fields, buttons, menus); font-display the titles and section headings, that is the parts the bold list names with the roles issue-title, title and section (STY-BOLD finds a rule of such a part that makes it bold without the display face); font-reader what a person reads at length (a description, a comment, the help of the search); font-mono code, issue IDs, the search language and time values. Every rule that sets a family names one of the four.
  • Cascadia Mono is first for code. Its regular weight draws with about a third more ink than the text face (M5 exit F-A1 measured 491 against 367 units for one line of 14 px), so code and IDs read a little heavier than the words around them. This is accepted to keep the sister project's stack exactly; STY-BOLD no longer refuses a font by its name, and it still refuses any bold weight the bold list does not name.
  • Measured, not assumed. The width of the ID column still comes from size-code-char, a probe drawn in the code font of the computer, so it is right for Cascadia Mono, Consolas or the system monospace face alike.

Update (M6, theme files like the sister project)

Decision of the maintainer (M6-Q1, M5-F167, M5-F121): the themes are handled the way the sister project handles them. Decisions 1, 2 and 6 read as follows; the rest stands.

  • A base and one file per theme. design/theme.kdl is the base theme, default: defaults, frame, variants, every token with its value and its more=, forced= and choice values, the contrast, distinct and bold rules, the mixins, keyframes, part rules and docs blocks. Its colors are those of Daylight, the light theme that starts. Each built-in theme is a file of design/themes/:

    theme "dusk" extends="default" kind="dark" {
    tokens {
        color "bg-canvas" "#1d2027"
        color "border" "#3b414d" more="#999ca2"
    }
}

    A theme file sets only the colors it changes (more= is its color for a device that asks for more contrast), so no value is written twice: Daylight's file is empty, and a theme that sets no color looks like Daylight. A line of a theme replaces the base's color and its more= together; a color the theme does not set keeps both from the base. A more= that is the color itself says nothing and is refused. With more contrast, a theme's block says again every color that the dark theme that starts changes there (the dark fallback of the device weighs as much as the theme's own block and comes after the theme's usual block, so a color its more-contrast block left out would be Dusk's), so a theme never shows Dusk's color for more contrast. forced= and the choices stay on the line of the base.

  • The file name is the theme's ID (dusk.kdl is the theme dusk, and the file says theme "dusk" so that it reads on its own; the reader refuses a file whose two names differ). The list of themes is the list of files: there is no themes block. The files are read in name order and listed light themes first, each kind in name order, which is the order of themeIds in tokens.ts, of the choices in themes.rs and of the blocks of the sheet. A new built-in theme is one new file (and its name in the message catalog); tokens.ts and themes.rs follow without any other change.

  • A token may name another token (M5-F121): color "hover-line" "$border-control". The sheet keeps the link as var(--border-control), so the browser follows it in every theme and mode; a theme file may give the token a color of its own (the dark themes give the hover line a brighter one) or name a source as well (Midnight's st-ns names fg-muted and has its own more=). STY-CONTRAST reads the color the link leads to, in each theme and mode; a link to a name that is no color token, and a loop, are errors of gen theme.

  • Shadows are the one other kind a theme sets. Today the shadow of a raised surface differs in shape between the themes (a ring in Midnight, a deeper drop in the dark themes), not only in color, so a theme file may set a shadow as well as a color. The maintainer accepted that a theme file sets its shadow as well as its colors (one shape for all four would have changed the look of Dusk and Midnight, and the split was to change nothing on screen). Whether the themes share one shape stays a question for the theme editor (M8). A theme file that sets any other kind of token, names a token the base does not have, sets a token twice or extends anything but default is an error of gen theme that names the file and the line.

  • One reader. Only cargo xtask gen theme reads the files (ThemeFile::load in xtask); the tests of the pictures of the front page read the colors from the generated sheet, not from KDL. The content security policy stays style-src 'self': the files are compiled at build time into the one static sheet, as decision 5 says.

  • Checks. STY-CONTRAST runs for every theme file and mode and names the theme's file in a finding; LINT-CSS and STY-TOKENS run again when a theme file changes; DOC-GENERATED compares the output of the base and the theme files.

Update (M8, themes of your own)

The maintainer's answers M8-Q8 to Q11 (2026-11-11). They settle decision 7 and leave the others as they are. The words are the glossary's: an own theme is a theme an organization or a person makes, for everyone or personal.

  • What an own theme may set (M8-Q10). The colours (each color token, with its more= colour), the shadow (the shadow token that a theme file may set, stored as its parts: offsets, blur, spread and a colour, at most two layers, never as text), the corner radius (r-ctl and r-card, within the bounds the base file gives them), and for the text faces font-ui, font-display and font-reader a choice among the system font stacks the base file already has (named by their token, never by a font name). Nothing else: no spacing, no Spacing, no text size, no motion, no font file and no rule, selector or CSS text. The list of tokens an own theme may set, with their kinds and bounds, is written by cargo xtask gen theme from the base file into Rust (crates/bb-core/src/theme/), so the server, the import and the editor read one list. THM-03 says so.
  • It starts from one built-in theme and stores only what it changes (M8-Q11). An own theme names the built-in theme it extends (Daylight, Paper, Dusk or Midnight) and takes its kind (light or dark) from it; it stores only the values it changes. The values it does not change are read from the built-in theme when its style sheet is made, so a later fix of a built-in theme (M7-F241) reaches it.
  • How it reaches the page (M8-Q8). The server makes one style sheet for each own theme from its stored values, with one writer in Rust, and serves it at /themes/{id}.css under the content security policy style-src 'self', which stays as it is (decision 5). The page links it with a link element when the person's choice is an own theme; the address carries the theme's version (?v=), so the browser keeps it as long as a hashed asset and a changed theme has a new address. The sheet sets the theme's variables under a frame attribute of its own (own in the frame line, written to the page as data-own-theme), on top of the built-in theme it extends, with its more= colours in a block for more contrast. A theme for everyone is served to every signed-in person of the organization, a personal theme only to its maker; any other request gets the answer of a theme that does not exist.
  • Contrast in one place (M8-Q9). The contrast maths (relative brightness, the ratio, CIE 1976 delta E) and the reading of the contrast and distinct rules move from the check in xtask into bb-core (crates/bb-core/src/contrast/, pure). gen theme writes the rules of the base file into Rust data beside it (DOC-GENERATED). STY-CONTRAST calls it for the built-in files, the server calls it when an own theme is saved or uploaded, and the theme editor calls it through the existing browser module bb-wasm, whose size PERF-BUNDLE holds. Each pair gets one rating: Easy when it passes the rule for more contrast (7:1 for text), OK when it passes its rule, Hard to read when it does not. A pair with no stricter rule is rated only OK or Hard to read: lines (whose minimum for more contrast is their usual minimum), the distinct pairs judged by delta E, and the category colors.
  • The draft of the editor. The unsaved values of the theme editor are kept on the server as the theme's draft and served by the same writer at /themes/{id}/draft.css?v=<n>, to its editor only; any other request gets the answer of a theme that does not exist. A new theme cannot be chosen until its first save; until then it is listed to its maker, and a theme for everyone also to the holders of Change organization settings, who may finish or delete it (marked saved: false). Save makes the draft the theme, so the preview needs no style made in the page. The sheet of a draft sets its variables only on the preview of the editor, an element that carries a sample of the built-in theme (preview in the frame line) and names the draft (draft, written as data-own-draft), never on the page; it writes the corners and the text faces even where the draft keeps those of the base, so a saved theme the page wears does not show through. The sheet of a saved theme also reaches a sample that names it (data-own-theme beside data-preview-look), in a block of its own that writes the corners and the faces as the draft's does, so a theme picker shows an own theme in its own colors and shapes and nothing of the page around it.
  • Saving. A theme for everyone cannot be saved while one of its pairs is Hard to read; the refusal names the pairs. A personal theme can be saved with a warning that names them (UX §5.6). An upload (JSON) is checked like a save: an unknown token or a value that its kind does not allow is refused with its name. Themes for everyone are made and changed by holders of Change organization settings (Organization settings › Look › Themes); any signed-in person makes personal themes (My settings › Appearance). The editor takes an edit lock on the theme (ADR-0019).
  • The choices of a theme. The settings Light theme and Dark theme list the built-in themes from the generated list (decision 6), then the organization's themes for everyone and the person's own personal themes of that kind. A choice that names an own theme which no longer exists, or which the person may no longer use, counts as the built-in theme it extended.
  • Checks. STY-CONTRAST grows from the built-in files to every own theme that is saved, with the same code. THEME-ONLY stays: the server's sheet is the only style that is not built from the theme files, and it holds variables only.
  • How it is built (WP-05). The routes are /api/v1/themes (list, make, read, save, take away, copy, file for a download, upload) and the two sheets /themes/{id}.css?v=<version> and /themes/{id}/draft.css?v=<n>, all in the API description, so SEC-MATRIX runs them for every starting role. A sheet whose address names the version it has now is kept private, max-age=31536000, immutable; an address with another version, or none, is asked again (private, no-cache). A theme is the look of a person in a browser: only a session reaches the routes, never an access key or an agent. The draft of the editor is the editing draft of ADR-0019 (one draft for each person and theme, kept by PUT /api/v1/drafts and the heartbeat, deleted by the save), so the draft sheet is made from the asking person's own draft and nobody else's draft can be served. A new theme, a copy and an upload count against the limits from the moment they are made, saved or not. A setting keeps the choice of an own theme as <built-in>/<id>: the server reads it and answers either the theme (own_theme in the setting's answer) or the built-in theme in its place; the browser parses nothing. The theme editor reads the readability of each pair from bb-wasm (theme_readability), the same bb_core::theme::readability the server rates a save with.

Consequences

  • A change of look is a change in the theme files (the base, or one theme's color file), and the generated sheet shows it in the diff. A rule exists once: the focus ring, the muted text, the field label.
  • Writing a component needs no CSS file and no class name. A style that the person's choices (spacing, text size, motion, contrast) cannot reach cannot be written.
  • cargo xtask gen theme is part of the build of the browser app and of DOC-GENERATED. The generated sheet is committed, so the server's embedded app needs no extra build step.
  • Specificity is that of attribute selectors, so the order in the file is the order in the sheet: a rule for a state is written after the rules for the variants it must win over. Enforced by: review (the order is seen in the diff of the file; the screenshots of the showcase show a change of look).
  • Rules for forced colors move to tokens (forced=) where one system color serves everywhere; a part keeps a forced { … } block where its own colors differ (a disabled button, a link).

Alternatives considered

  • Keep JSON (design/theme.json): no new dependency, but no comments, long, and the variants of a value would not sit on one line. KDL was chosen.
  • The sister project's way, compiling in the browser: needs a style element or adoptedStyleSheets from a string, which style-src 'self' forbids. Rejected.
  • Keep CSS Modules next to the token file: the situation of the audit. Rejected.
  • A hand-written style sheet with the same data attributes: the values and the rules would again be in two places that no tool joins, and the theme list could not be generated from it.
  • Tailwind CSS and CSS-in-JS at run time: rejected in ADR-0010 and still.

Enforced by

THEME-ONLY (no style=, no className, no CSS file but the generated one), STY-TOKENS (no color written out), STY-PARTS (every part a rule names is a part some component has), LINT-CSS (the compiled rules use token variables only), STY-CONTRAST (every theme and mode), STY-BOLD (bold only for the parts the bold list of the file names, UX §7.3; titles and headings in the display face), DOC-GENERATED (the sheet, the names and the theme choices are the output of the file).

ADR-0027: Layouts, rules per issue type and the starting workflow

Status: Accepted · 2026-10-09

Context

M3 brings issue types (ISS-02), layouts for the issue page and the new-issue form (CFG-01), field levels per issue type (SEC-04, UX §5.2 More options), kinds of relation (ISS-04) and own fields (CF-03). All of these are set for the whole organization or a project, and some also for one issue type. The settings registry (ADR-0018) has the layers default → organization → nearest project → person, but no issue type, and a layout is a structure, not a value. Workflows come in M4, yet every issue needs a status from the start.

Decision

  1. Own tables, settings-like lookup. Layouts, field levels per issue type and kinds of relation live in their own tables, not in the settings registry. Each row names its place (the organization or a project) and optionally an issue type.
  2. One lookup order, defined once: for a project and an issue type, the nearest place with a row wins (the project, then its parents, then the organization); at one place, a row for the issue type wins over a row for all types. The lookup is one function in bb-core, used by layouts and by field levels; a sub-project uses its parent's layout until it gets its own.
  3. Field levels per issue type join the evaluation of architecture §7 (step 7) through that lookup; a level for a type is set under More options on the field-permission page.
  4. Layouts never widen permissions. A layout decides where a field shows and for which roles; a field shows only if the layout lists it for one of the person's roles and the field level lets them see it (to fill it in on the new-issue form: change it).
  5. The starting workflow (decision M3-Q1): one workflow, defined once in bb-core, with Open (status group Not started), In progress (In progress) and Done (Done); every status can follow every other; entering a status of the Done group sets the closed date and leaving it clears it. Every issue type uses it until M4, whose workflow editor makes it the first workflow of the organization; stored statuses keep their IDs.
  6. Editors lock. The layout editor takes an edit lock (ADR-0019) while open, like the workflow and theme editors.

Consequences

  • Own fields, layouts and per-type levels follow one inheritance rule people learn once.
  • The settings registry stays a registry of single values; structures have their own tables and migrations.
  • M4 replaces the starting workflow without a data migration of issues.

Amendment, M3 WP-05: field levels per issue type

The lookup of decision 2 is bb_core::lookup::nearest_row: the one function that finds the row for a place and an issue type. The levels of fields per issue type use it today (bb_policy::nearest_typed_rule, which nearest_rule for the plain levels also calls); layouts (WP-09) use the same function.

  • Storage. A level for one issue type is a row in role_type_field_level (the role's own) or project_type_field_level (set for a project), next to the tables of the levels for all types. The rows join the evaluation as LevelRules::typed; they are read together with the other levels of the roles at a place.
  • Reading. Evaluation::field_level_for(issue_type, field) is the level of a field on an item of that type, field_mask_for the mask. A view that holds its issue type (#[masked(item_type)]) is masked with the mask of that type; a view that does not say its type gets, for each field, the lowest level the field has in any type, so a field that is hidden for some type is never shown by a view that does not say which type it is for.
  • Setting. The route of the field permissions takes ?issue_type=; taking a level for a type away is allowed at the organization too (the role's own level for all types always exists).
  • Names of own fields. A screen that names fields (Field permissions, Check access, the move preview) lists an own field, and prints its name, only for a viewer who may know the field: they may see it in some issue type (any level above Hidden), or they have Manage fields, because whoever manages fields reads every definition on the Fields settings page anyway. For every other viewer the field's name, its ID and its rows are left out of the answer. Values are another matter: a value follows the level of its field, and Manage fields gives no right to read one. The rule is may_know in bb-app (fields/catalogue.rs); the move preview applies it per project of a row, so a field for a sub-project keeps its name for a viewer who may know it there.
  • Naming people in a field. One rule, may_name in bb-app (access/candidates.rs), decides whether a person can be put into Assigned to or into an own field of people, and which people the list to choose from offers: the person exists, the viewer is shown people by name (Assigned to and Project members both show names, ADR-0022) or names themselves, and the person may see the item. A viewer who is shown others only as a role has no ID to name them by, so the ID of somebody else sent in a request is refused alike for a person who is there and one who is not. A value the field holds already, or that Undo puts back, skips only the access of the person named; the person still has to exist.
  • Names of tags. The settings list of tags (Organization settings › Labels & tags) follows the same rule as the names of own fields and projects: a tag is listed, and can be changed, renamed or combined, only for a person who may know the tag: it has no limit, or it is limited to a project they see, or it is used in one. A tag only projects they cannot see know is not there for them (resource.not-found), and the answer never says that a hidden limit exists: a tag with limits only to hidden projects reads as for every project. Saving the projects of a tag replaces only the limits on projects the person sees; the limits on projects they cannot see stay, so a person never drops a limit they cannot see, and an empty list from such a person never makes a tag that is limited to hidden projects a tag for the whole organization. The rule is known_tags in bb-app (tags/manage.rs); the tests are tag_01_the_settings_list_leaves_out_a_tag_only_a_hidden_project_knows, tag_01_saving_the_projects_keeps_the_limits_on_projects_the_person_cannot_see and tag_01_an_empty_list_from_such_a_person_does_not_create_the_tag_organization_wide.

Amendment, M3 WP-09: layouts

  • Storage. layout (where it is set: a project or the organization, an issue type or all, and the form: new-issue or issue-page), layout_section, layout_field and layout_field_role (migration 12). A layout is saved as a whole on the version the editor looked at.
  • Lookup. bb_core::layout::find is nearest_row, the same walk as for field levels. Until somebody customizes a form no row exists and LayoutContent::starting counts. Customize makes a row as a copy of the layout in force.
  • Reading. form_layout applies the layout to the roles of the person and to the levels of the fields: the rule is layouts::effective, which asks the mask and the own-field functions of the field use cases (changeable_own_fields, visible_own_fields) and restates no level. A required own field stays on the new-issue form for everybody who can fill it in.
  • Editing. The editor needs Manage issue types, kinds of relation and layouts at the place, holds an edit lock on the layout (part layout), and saves through save_text, so a lost lock or an old version keeps the sections as a draft. Own fields the editor may not know are left out of the editor and kept on save (may_know).
  • Drafts. The draft a refused save keeps holds only what the editor sent, never the own fields that were put back for it (may_know), so a draft cannot show the ID of a field the person may not know. The event and the write hold the whole layout.
  • Size. A layout holds at most PLACED_MAX fields: the most own fields (own_fields::FIELDS_MAX) plus the most built-in fields of a form, so the starting layout of any organization can be stored. Customize checks the copy like a save does.
  • Roles in the editor. Role names, the per-role marks "field permissions win" and the tick boxes need Decide what roles see at the place (the permission the Field permissions page needs); somebody with only Manage issue types, kinds of relation and layouts gets the editor with choose_roles: false, no role names and no marks. Their save does not change roles: a field that is on the layout keeps its roles, and a field that is added is shown to every role, unless it was on the layout before and was taken off: a field taken off keeps its roles (table layout_off_field, migration 19, one row for each field of the layout that is off the form, its roles still in layout_field_role), so putting it back shows it to the same roles (M4 WP-09, M3-F107). The list of roles is cut at ROLES_MAX (100) like the table of field permissions.
  • Taking a layout away. Refused with edit.in-progress while somebody else holds its edit lock (the page names who, with the people levels of the reader, from the lock); a lock of the person's own is let go in the same change.
  • Required. One function, must_be_asked_for (required and without a default), decides for the server (a new issue without a value is refused), for the form a person gets and for the "required" mark in the editor.

Amendment, M4 WP-11: issue types and groups of labels per project

  • Where something is offered is data. A row of offer (migration 18) says, for one issue type or one group of labels and one place (a project, or the whole organization), whether it is offered there. One definition of the answer, bb_core::offer::is_offered, uses bb_core::lookup::nearest_row (the walk of layouts and workflows): the nearest place with a row wins, and a project follows its parent until it has a row of its own. No row means offered everywhere, so an upgraded database offers what it offered before.
  • Where it was created. An issue type and a group of labels get the project they were created in (none for the whole organization; the ones that were there keep none). A subject created in a project is offered there and below until a row below it says otherwise; a row above it, or for the whole organization, is no part of the answer.
  • Who manages what is judged at a place. Manage issue types, kinds of relation and layouts and Manage labels and tags are judged where the type or the group was created (creating, renaming, retiring, and the labels in a group), and a row of the offers where the row is for. A Project lead therefore manages what they created in their projects, and can switch a type or a group of the whole organization off in their own projects and below, and nowhere else. A subject created in a project takes rows for that project and below only. Combining two labels needs the permission for both groups. A key never holds either permission.
  • One change of the offers is made whole or not at all, inside one change that counts the version of the subject up, so a person who looked at an old state is told (edit.version-changed). It takes the lock of the workflows alone (lock_workflows), and so does retiring an issue type; creating, changing and moving an issue, and putting a label on one, take it shared (lock_chain_in, then ensure_type_takes_issues_in or group_offers_in judge the offers again), so no issue gets a type or a label that a change of the offers has taken away meanwhile. The order of the locks is LockClass in bb-store (ARCH-LOCK-ORDER).
  • A Project lead of P changes what the projects under P are offered, and may switch a type of the organization back on. A row for a project is judged at that project, and a person who holds the permission in P holds it in every project below P, also in one where they have No access for everything else (the permission to look after types and labels is not a right to see issues). So a lead of P can switch a type off or on for a sub-project of P that they cannot see, and can switch an organization type that an administrator switched off for the whole organization back on in their own projects (a row at P is nearer than the row for the organization). That is the decision, confirmed in the review of WP-11. Two leads who change the rows of one type at the same moment are told by the version of the type (edit.version-changed): the second one looks again.
  • Who may know a subject. The name of a type or a group created in a project is not told to everybody who is signed in. One rule (offers/known.rs) decides it for the lists, the rows of the offers, Check access and every use case that takes a type or a group by its ID: a subject created for the whole organization is known to everyone; one created in a project is known to a person who may know that project (the one definition of the policy, Evaluation::knows_project: they see it or decide who has which role there) or who sees a project inside it (a visible sub-project under a hidden parent is told what the parent created and what reaches it), or when it is used on an issue they read (for a group of labels: on an issue whose labels their role lets them see, as for a tag, SEC-06). Anything else is resource.not-found, exactly like one that is not there. A key sees what its project narrows it to. A label is known with its group. A list about a project (?project=) holds only the subjects that can reach it (bb_core::offer::reaches). The editors of layouts and workflows, the catalogue of fields and an issue written with a type apply the same rule; the types of an issue the person reads are known by use. The lists of labels and of groups of labels are lists like the others: paged, with fields= and a page-size cap (GET /api/v1/labels and GET /api/v1/label-groups).
  • Names. A name is unique among the subjects that can meet in one project: those created for the whole organization, and those created in the same chain of projects (the project, the projects above it and those below it); siblings may use one name. A subject of the organization stays unique against all subjects. A clash with a subject the person may not know still answers name.taken; that is accepted, and it reaches only the person's own chain (bb_core::offer::can_meet; migration 18 takes the unique key of the names of groups away, the program judges it inside the change). The name of a label is unique in its group.
  • Limits are counted for each place. A place has at most ISSUE_TYPES_MAX types, LABEL_GROUPS_MAX groups and LABELS_MAX labels of the groups created there (the labels in no group, and the organization's, are the organization's); a project that is full does not use up the room of another.
  • A rename that reaches other projects. A label stays on an issue that moved out of the project of its group. Renaming or combining such a label rewrites those issues, so a person who does not hold Manage labels and tags for the whole organization is refused (access.forbidden, without a number) when an issue of a project they do not look after has the label.
  • The rows a reader gets leave out places they may not know, and the event of a change of the offers names only the places that were changed.
  • Issues keep what they have. A new issue, and a change of the type of an issue, refuse a type that is retired (issue.type-retired) or that the project does not offer (issue.type-not-offered); a label of a group the project does not offer is not put on an issue (label.not-offered). An issue that has a type or a label keeps it. Moving an issue never counts a retired or an unused type as missing (M3-F124): the preview names it ("{type} is not used in {project}"), no run is skipped for type-missing any more (the word stays readable in runs that were stored), and label-not-here is the reason for a label put on an issue by a change to many issues.
  • Check access per issue type (M3-F44). Evaluation::explain_level_for and report_for give the level of a field for one issue type with the reason of each role, found the way field_level_for finds it. The answer says differs_by_type (some type has a level for some field that the all-types answer does not, among the fields the reader may know), and the screen asks Which issue type? only then.

Alternatives considered

  • Layouts as settings values (JSON in the registry): no issue-type dimension, no typed validation, and every reader would parse JSON. Rejected.
  • Fixed statuses with no workflow model: M4 would have to migrate every issue. Rejected.

Enforced by

Review (the lookup function is the one place; its property test cfg_01_a_layout_never_shows_a_field_the_role_cannot_see lives in WP-09) and SEC-MATRIX for the levels per issue type.

ADR-0028: The message catalog is split into parts; the first page loads one

Status: Accepted · 2026-10-13

Context

messages/en.json is the one source of every word (UX-07). The browser got all of it as one object, so every text of every screen was in the first page, and each new screen made the first page bigger: the catalog was about 22 KB of the 250 KB the first page may have (PERF-04, ADR-0009). The next package in line already pushed the first page over the budget through new texts alone.

Decision

  1. en.json stays the one source, and the generator writes the parts. cargo xtask gen messages writes one TypeScript file per part into web/packages/messages/src/generated/: shared.ts (the first page) and one file per folder of web/app/src/features/, plus types.ts (the type of every key, with no text in it) and all.ts (every part, for tests).
  2. One rule says where a key goes, and nobody keeps a list of keys. Code names a key when it writes it as a string, or builds it from a template (`issue-field.${code}` or "issue-field." + code): a template names every key that starts with its text. Comments do not count. A key goes to the part of a feature when that feature is the only code that names it (the same reading TXT-CATALOG uses for "used"). It goes to shared when code outside the features names it, when two features do, and when no code names it: the server sends such a key, or a word of an enum makes it, and then any page may show it. The keys that the words of the enums make (error codes, issue-field., starting-role., permissions and so on, from one list that the generator and TXT-CATALOG share) are always shared, whatever the code says: the server sends them by key and shared code looks them up at run time. The one table in the generator lists the parts (shared and the feature folders); it stays a table, because the paths of generated files are known without reading the folders (META-COVERAGE counts them). A test and TXT-CATALOG compare it with the folders, so a new feature cannot be forgotten (its texts would stay on the first page until it is added). A new key therefore starts on the first page and moves to its area as soon as the area's code names it; the diff of the generated files shows it.
  3. t() stays synchronous and keeps its types. Every part registers its texts when its file is loaded (registry.ts). The entry of a feature (index.ts) imports its part as its first import, so the part lands in the chunk of that feature and is evaluated before the feature runs. Routes load a feature with import() before they render it, so the texts are there; a screen that sits behind OnlyWith has a route loader (loadsScreen) that loads it first, because the router cannot see a lazy component inside another one. isMessageKey is true for loaded keys only, which is why the code that looks keys up by a string lives in the area whose part holds them, or the keys are on the first page. A text that is not loaded is a defect of the build, and a person never sees a key. While the app is built for development (import.meta.env.DEV, which vitest sets too) t() throws with the key in the message, so the defect is found at once. In production t() writes console.error once per key, naming the key, and returns an empty text, so the rest of the page keeps working. The end-to-end tests fail a test on any console.error of the app (the shared fixture; the browser's own "Failed to load resource" lines for refused requests do not count), so the defect is still found before release. The vitest tests cannot find a part that an area forgot to import, because they load every part; TXT-CATALOG finds it.
  4. Outside the browser app everything is loaded. @bugaboo/messages resolves to an entry that loads every part for Node (unit tests and end-to-end tests); the browser build resolves to the plain entry.
  5. Precompiling the messages at build time is not done now. It would let the first page drop the ICU parser (about 57 KB of source, some 8 KB after Brotli), but it needs the ICU syntax tree written by the generator and an alias of the parser in the build and not in the tests. Splitting the catalog gives the room that was asked for; the parser can go later, as its own decision.

Consequences

  • The first page carries the texts of the shell, sign-in, setup and errors shown anywhere, plus the texts of the features that the first page itself loads. A feature that is loaded lazily brings its texts in its own chunk; the texts of the rest of M3 and beyond land there too.
  • cargo xtask gen messages now reads the code of web/ as well as the catalog. DOC-GENERATED fails when a change of code moves a key, and gen messages fixes it.
  • A feature that the first page loads statically (today shell, sign-in, home; account became lazy in M8, when the page that sets up the second step started to load it on first use) keeps its texts on the first page. Making such a feature lazy moves its texts with it.
  • A text that two lazy features show is on the first page. That is cheap for common words and a reason to name such a text once in shared code.

Alternatives considered

  • A table from the first part of a key (its area) to a part. Simple, but a key shown by two areas (a projects. text that the issues screens also show) cannot be placed, and the table drifts from the code.
  • Load a part asynchronously from t(). Makes t() asynchronous at every call site. Rejected.
  • One chunk per area chosen by hand in the build configuration. A second list of areas that nothing checks. Rejected.

Enforced by

DOC-GENERATED (the parts are the output of the catalog and the code), TXT-CATALOG (every feature folder has a part, the entry of every feature with texts imports its part as its first import statement, in code and not in a comment, and nothing else does), the end-to-end fixture (a console.error of the app fails the test), PERF-BUNDLE (the first page stays within its budget), LINT-TYPES (every key keeps its type), and the tests in web/packages/messages (every key is in exactly one part, a key is found once its part is loaded, a missing text fails).

ADR-0029: AI agents: apps that act for a person, and agents that work on their own

Status: Accepted · 2026-10-16 · refines ADR-0013 and ADR-0025

Context

M7 plans the MCP server (AI-20…AI-23): an outside AI app signs in as a person and does what that person may do (AI-04). Decision: this stays, and agents should also be able to work on their own, with a person's permission, on chosen issues. Bugaboo does not run agents, now or in the foreseeable future: they run outside (coding agents in a developer's tools, a company's own agents) and connect through MCP.

An agent works on an issue differently from a person:

PersonAgent
The issueA reminder and a conversation; much of the context is in people's headsThe whole job: it knows nothing that is not written there or linked from it
MemoryRemembers yesterdayStarts fresh each time; what it learned must be stored
How work goesSteady, with a comment now and thenIn attempts: plan, work, result or failure, try again; several at once
When stuckAsks someoneAsks through the issue and waits, or guesses
Done"Looks fine to me"Checkable: tests pass, what Done when says is true
What it leavesA comment, a new statusA branch, a pull request, a test report, a log, its time and cost
TrustEarned over yearsEvery result is reviewed by a person
PaceOne issue at a timeHundreds of reads and changes in minutes, often unattended

One person may also drive several agents at the same time, each on its own issues.

Decision

1. Two ways in, one policy engine

  • An AI app acting for a person (AI-04, AI-22, AI-23, unchanged): the app signs in as the person through OAuth or an access key, does at most what the person may do, narrowed by the key's choice, and the history says "Ada Brandt via Claude Code". This is the way for "give all my open issues in Website to Lea".
  • An agent working on its own (AI-30): an account of its own that is not a person. It can do nothing until a person gives it work (decision 3).
  • Both go through bb-policy and the one tool registry of ADR-0013; there is no second rule set. Enforced by: ARCH-AI-TOOLS and SEC-MATRIX (rows for the actor kinds person via app and agent).

2. Agents

  • Every agent has one responsible person, normally the person who made it; handing an agent to another person needs that person's acceptance. Creating agents takes the new permission Create agents that work for you, a project permission of kind Change that Administrator, Project lead and Team member hold at the start (M7-Q1, amendment M7): a person who holds it in at least one project may create agents, and an agent may be handed issues or given a standing rule only in the projects where its person holds it, so a project lead decides where agents work. Administrators see every agent of the organization in Organization settings › Connections › Agents and can stop any of them; an administrator can switch agents off for the organization or a project, like AI itself (AI-02). Enforced by: the tests ai_30_an_agent_needs_a_responsible_person and ai_30_an_administrator_stops_any_agent (M7).
  • What an agent can do at a place is at most what its responsible person can do there, narrowed by its work (decision 3) and its limits (decision 9). When the person loses that access, is switched off or leaves, the agent loses it at the next request, and its open work becomes Stopped. Enforced by: the tests ai_30_an_agent_never_does_more_than_its_person and ai_30_an_agent_stops_when_its_person_loses_access (M7).
  • An agent is not a member: it has no role, is in no group, never appears in Who has which role, and is never Assigned to an issue. The issue keeps its person; while an agent works on it the issue shows "worked on by Fixer". This keeps a person answerable for every issue and keeps COMP-10 simple. Enforced by: the tests ai_30_an_agent_cannot_be_assigned and ai_30_an_agent_has_no_role (M7).
  • Shown as its name with an agent mark and its person: "Fixer, agent of Ada Brandt". Its own name is always shown (it is not a person); its person follows Who sees people for the viewer ("agent of Someone (Team member)").
  • An agent signs in with its own agent key (an access key that belongs to the agent and always runs out) or with OAuth for its app. Agent keys are listed with the agent and can be renewed or taken back there.
  • One person, several agents: a person may have several agents, and each agent may work on several issues at once, within its limits. My agents (decision 8) shows all of them together, with what waits for the person first.

3. Giving an agent work: hand over, or a standing rule

There are two ways, and no third one (a project-wide permission would be a standing rule without a filter).

  • Hand over (AI-31): a person hands one or several issues, by their IDs, to one of their agents in the Hand over to an agent window. They choose:

    • the agent;
    • the brief: taken from the issue (description, Steps to reproduce, Done when), plus a note; the window says what is missing ("No steps to reproduce") but does not stop the hand-over;
    • what the agent may do in Bugaboo: always read the issue and what it links to, comment, report its work and the time and cost it spent (on its attempt, never as a time entry: decision 4), attach results and link related issues; ticked on request: change named fields, change the status, make sub-issues;
    • a budget: attempts, time, and the cost the agent reports;
    • whether its plan needs approval before it starts.

    The hand-over ends at Accept, Throw away, Stop, or when it runs out (14 days unless set otherwise). The person handing over needs Change issues (or Change the issues they reported) on each issue, and Create agents that work for you in its project (M7-Q1). Enforced by: the tests ai_31_a_handed_over_agent_sees_only_its_issues and ai_31_a_hand_over_ends_at_accept (M7).

  • Standing rule (AI-32): a person lets one of their agents work on everything a saved search finds, for example "every new bug in Website". Because anybody who changes an issue so that it matches gives the agent that issue, a standing rule has two ways, and the first is narrow:

    • Propose (the default): the agent reads what the rule finds and proposes; nothing changes until a person clicks Apply, as with the assistant. It may create issues in one named project when the rule says so (for an agent that reports failing tests). It never changes an issue it was not handed (the amendment "A change needs an attempt that runs");
    • Hand over what it finds (amendment "Rules that hand over"): each issue the rule finds becomes a hand-over to the agent, once, with the rules of every hand-over;
    • it never changes a field that holds people (Assigned to, Followers, Reported by) and never the status unless a hand-over ticks it. Enforced by: the test ai_32_a_standing_rule_never_changes_people_fields (M7), and COMP-10 in review;
    • it runs out after 30 days unless set otherwise (at most 90) and is renewed with one click; an administrator can allow rules that never run out (the amendment "Rules that hand over");
    • every issue that newly comes under the rule is written down, so the person sees what the agent saw.

  • Never given to an agent: the permissions of kind Manage (people, roles, settings, fields) and Take over text someone else is editing. Enforced by: the test ai_30_an_agent_never_holds_a_manage_permission (M7).

4. Agent work: the record of what the agent does on an issue

  • Agent work (AI-33) is a record of its own on the issue, apart from the comments, so the conversation stays readable for people. It holds the brief, the attempts (each with the agent's plan, its steps, its results as links such as a branch, a pull request or a test report, and the time and cost the agent reports, marked as reported by the agent), the questions and their answers, and the review.
  • An agent's time is not working time (M7-Q7). The time and cost an agent reports stay on its attempt, marked as reported by the agent. An agent never makes a time entry, and no total of Time spent counts what it reports (ADR-0035, decisions 4 and 9). An AI app acting for a person may book that person's own time (log_time, AI-21), with the person's Book time. Enforced by: the test ai_33_an_agent_never_makes_a_time_entry (WP-08) and SEC-MATRIX.
  • States, shown on the issue page, as a mark on list rows (the row keeps its status color) and searchable (agent is Fixer, agent state is "waiting-for-you", written as the search language writes a filter): Waiting for the agent, Agent working, Waiting for you (a question or a plan to approve), Ready for review, Agent gave up, Stopped.
  • When an attempt is ready, one short comment marked Written by an agent says so and links to the agent work.
  • The issue's own status is not an agent state. It moves only through the review (decision 6).

5. Questions back, instead of guessing

  • An agent that is stuck asks (MCP tool ask). Its work waits as Waiting for you; the responsible person and the person who handed it over get a notification (NTF-01). The answer is stored in the brief, so the next attempt and any other agent read it. Enforced by: the test ai_34_a_question_waits_for_an_answer_and_the_answer_joins_the_brief (M7).
  • With Plan needs approval, the first step of each attempt is the plan, and the agent waits for Approve plan or a note.

6. Review

  • At Ready for review a person chooses Accept (the hand-over ends; the status moves to the one the reviewer picks, proposed by the workflow), Send back with a note (a new attempt with the note in the brief) or Throw away (everything the attempts changed in Bugaboo is undone in one step; results outside Bugaboo, such as a branch, are the agent's business, and the window says so).
  • A project can allow Accept by itself when its checks pass for handed-over issues (off at the start). Issues accepted that way are listed under Accepted by itself in My agents until a person has looked at them.
  • What "its checks pass" means (M7-Q8). An agent attaches results of the kind Check with passed or failed (MCP tool attach). An attempt is accepted by itself only when the project allows it, the hand-over has it ticked (the tick is off in the window at the start; amendment M7-F227), the attempt has at least one check, and every check of the attempt passed. Bugaboo does not run or verify outside checks, and the hand-over window says so. The status after such an accept is the one the workflow proposes. Enforced by: the tests ai_35_accept_by_itself_is_off_at_the_start and ai_35_an_attempt_without_a_check_or_with_a_failed_one_waits_for_a_person (WP-08).

7. Runs: everything an app or an agent did, undone together

  • Every session of an AI app acting for a person, and every attempt of an agent, is one run (AI-38), built on the store of changes to many issues (change_run, its events and its Stopped state). A run is shown as the list of its changes and can be undone in one step; a change that somebody changed again afterwards is skipped and named, as in Change many issues. Enforced by: the test ai_38_a_run_is_undone_in_one_step_and_skips_later_changes (M7).
  • Text written through MCP is marked Written by an AI app or Written by an agent, stored with the text like Written with the assistant (COMP-08, COMP-09).

8. My agents: one person, several agents

  • My agents (AI-37) lists the person's agents and all their work at once. On top is what waits for the person (questions, plans to approve, results to review, standing rules about to run out), then the work in progress per agent, then the standing rules. Each agent can be paused or stopped, and Stop all my agents stops every one in one step.
  • On a phone, My agents shows Waiting for you first, so questions and reviews can be answered on the way.

9. Built for agents: tools, limits, safety

  • MCP tools for agents (AI-36), in the one tool registry: take an issue that is handed over (all or nothing, with the issue's version, so two agents never start the same work), report a step, ask, attach a result, give up with a reason, and changes since (what changed in the issues it may see since a mark it got before). Every write tool takes preview and then answers what would happen, from the same one evaluation as the preview of Change many issues. Each tool says whether it only reads or changes something. Enforced by: ARCH-AI-TOOLS (every tool declares read or change and has a preview test).
  • Long texts: agents never hold an edit lock for longer than one save and never take over a person's text; a save against an older version is refused with the newer text, as for people (Compare and save). Enforced by: the test ai_36_an_agent_never_takes_over_a_lock (M7).
  • Limits per agent and per key: changes per minute, issues at once, attempts per issue; the defaults are in the amendment M7. Reaching a limit pauses the agent with a sentence; it never drops a change halfway.
  • Untrusted text: tool answers mark every text with who wrote it (the author marks of ADR-0013, amendment M7), so the agent's own safeguards can treat it as data, not as instructions (AI-05). The prompt-injection test set covers agents and standing rules.
  • COMP-10: no tool ranks, evaluates or picks people. An app acting for a person may assign issues because the person told it to; an agent working on its own never changes a field that holds people (decision 3).

10. Agents of the organization (V1)

  • AUTH-08 (V1, M12) becomes agents of the organization: the same model, with the organization as the responsible party and a role instead of a person's rights, for webhooks (NTF-03) and imports. It is built on this decision, not beside it.

Amendment (M7, the maintainer's answers M7-Q1, Q7 and Q8, and the defaults)

The maintainer accepted every recommendation of M7-Q1 to Q10 on 2026-11-07. Decisions 2, 3, 4 and 6 above are written with the answers; what they add:

  • Who may create agents (M7-Q1): Create agents that work for you is a project permission (decision 2), not an organization one: an organization permission counts only from a role given for the whole organization (ADR-0025, decision 1), and Project lead and Team member are given on projects, so nearly nobody would have held it. The catalogue entry is in ADR-0025, amendment M7. Enforced by: ARCH-PERMS, and the test ai_30_an_agent_works_only_where_its_person_may_create_agents (WP-04).
  • NOT_FOR_AGENTS: what an agent never holds (decision 3) is one list in bb-policy, beside NOT_FOR_KEYS. Enforced by: ARCH-PERMS.
  • The limits of an agent (decision 9) start at 60 changes a minute, 5 issues at once and 5 attempts on one issue. Each is a value of the agent (on its page), at most the organization's maximum, which is a setting under Organization settings › Connections › Agents (ADR-0018, amendment M7) and starts at the same numbers; an agent key counts toward its agent's limits. Enforced by: ARCH-SETTINGS, and the tests of WP-09.
  • Proposals of a standing rule are records on the issue's agent work (before and after, the agent, the rule), which a person applies or discards through the same path as the assistant's Apply; nothing changes until then. Enforced by: TEST-PROMPT-INJECTION (the standing-rule cases) and the tests of WP-08.
  • The time of an agent (M7-Q7) and its checks (M7-Q8) are decisions 4 and 6.
  • The status after an accept by itself (decision 6). When an attempt is accepted by itself, the issue moves to the one status of the Done group that the workflow allows from its current status, through the workflow's own change, when exactly one exists. When none or several exist, or the change is not let through, the issue keeps its status and the agent work says "Accepted; choose the next status" until a person has looked at it. Enforced by: the tests ai_35_after_an_accept_by_itself_the_issue_moves_to_the_one_done_status_the_workflow_allows and ai_35_with_several_done_statuses_the_status_stays_and_the_person_is_told (WP-08).
  • Throw away undoes the run of every attempt, newest first, as the reviewer, each change judged again; a change somebody made since is skipped and named by the undo itself. Enforced by: ai_35_throw_away_undoes_every_attempt_in_one_step (WP-08).
  • A change needs an attempt that runs (M7-F120). An agent changes a field, the description, tags, labels, relations, files, comments or the parent of an issue it was handed only while an attempt of it runs on that issue, and the change belongs to the run of that attempt (decision 7). While the work is Waiting for the agent (before take) or Ready for review (after submit), no attempt runs and the change is refused with access.forbidden; otherwise Throw away could not undo it. The one change without an attempt is the move of the status that follows an accept by itself: the system makes it, not the agent. Issues that only a standing rule found have no hand-over, so no attempt and no run: the agent reads them and proposes (decision 3) and changes nothing there, whatever fields the rule names (the fields of a rule add to what a hand-over of the same issue allows, and to nothing else). The option Change only these fields of a standing rule therefore changes nothing and goes away: a rule that hands over what it finds, so that the agent works in attempts with runs, comes with WP-14 of M7. Enforced by: the tests m7_f120_an_agent_changes_a_handed_issue_only_while_an_attempt_runs, m7_f120_a_change_over_mcp_needs_an_attempt_that_runs and m7_f120_an_agent_changes_nothing_on_an_issue_only_a_standing_rule_found.
  • Agents of the organization (decision 10, AUTH-08) stay in M12, and Bugaboo runs no agents (M7-Q10).
  • Accept by itself needs the tick on the hand-over (M7-F227). Decision 6 read as if an attempt were accepted by itself unless the hand-over turned it off. What is built, and what the hand-over window and the user documents say, is the other way round: the tick Accept by itself when its checks pass is off in the window at the start, and an attempt is accepted by itself only when the project allows it and the hand-over has the tick. This text replaces the older reading.
  • Preview over MCP (M7-F225). Decision 9 says every write tool takes preview. Over MCP the server offers it as the boolean argument preview in the input schema of every tool that changes something and of no tool that reads (offered in bb-mcp/src/methods.rs, from the effect the registry names). true calls the tool in preview mode: the same before and after as the assistant's proposal, nothing saved, no entry of a run, the same rights, it counts toward the same limit of calls and is not counted as a change, and the log of tool calls marks it as a read. The answer of the call that saves differs from the preview: it says changed where the preview says would_change, and ends with one line that names what was saved and its version (Saved in bb-app/src/ai/tools/call.rs); a new issue is named by its internal ID, its readable ID and its version, because the search finds it only after the next round of the jobs (ADR-0016). Enforced by: the tests ai_21_a_saved_change_over_mcp_says_changed_and_its_version_where_the_preview_would, ai_21_an_app_that_creates_an_issue_is_told_its_id_its_readable_id_and_its_version, m7_f225_a_preview_is_offered_on_change_tools_only, m7_f225_a_preview_over_mcp_changes_nothing_and_the_same_call_without_it_does, m7_f225_a_preview_of_what_the_caller_may_not_change_is_refused_like_a_run and m7_f225_the_log_marks_a_preview_of_a_change_as_a_read.

Amendment (M7, WP-14): rules that hand over, and rules with no end

The maintainer decided on 2026-11-09 that Bugaboo must be able to run agents with no person in the loop. What it changes in decision 3:

  • A rule has a way of working (RuleWay): Propose changes (the old default) or Hand over what it finds. The way is fixed when the rule is made.
  • Hand over what it finds. Each issue the rule's saved search finds, now and later, inside the rule's project and the rights its person holds now, becomes one hand-over of that issue to the rule's agent. The hand-over is made by the same code as a hand-over by a person (plan_hand_over), with the rule's powers (the ticks and named fields of the hand-over window), the agent's limit of attempts as the budget, no plan approval, Accept by itself left to the project, the usual end (14 days), one taker, and its event. The agent takes it and works in attempts, each with a run, so Throw away and Undo the run stay complete. The person must hold what a hand-over needs when the rule looks (Change issues, Create agents that work for you, agents on); an issue they cannot hand over then is left out and looked at again later.
  • Once per issue. The match record of the rule is the memory: a rule hands an issue over when it first comes under it and never again, not after the hand-over ended and not when the issue changes and matches again (a rule must not trigger itself through the changes of its own agent). An issue that already has open work of the agent is written down and not handed over twice. A person can hand it over again or send it back.
  • The limits cap the flood. A rule hands over only while the agent has fewer open pieces of work than its limit Issues at once; the others are looked at again when room is made (the notification round that sees a hand-over end, work stopped or given up, or a review that ends work queues the look for the projects of the agent's rules that hand over) and at the next change of an issue in the project. Enforced by: m7_wp14_the_limit_of_the_agent_caps_the_open_hand_overs_of_a_rule.
  • "Change only these fields" is dropped. On an issue that only a rule found, an agent reads and proposes and changes nothing (the amendment "A change needs an attempt that runs"), so the option had no effect left. It is removed from the window, the API, the docs and the glossary; a rule made with it is migrated to Propose. Enforced by: m7_wp14_a_migrated_rule_proposes and m7_f120_an_agent_changes_nothing_on_an_issue_only_a_standing_rule_found.
  • Rules that never run out. A rule keeps 30 days by default and 90 days at most (the bound of the setting agents.rule-days). The organization setting agents.rules-never-run-out (Allow rules that never run out, administrators only, off at the start; ADR-0018) lets a person choose Never runs out. Such a rule can be stopped at any time and the limits of its agent still apply. Switching the setting off gives each rule that never runs out an end at the most days (90) from then, with the usual warning (the job agents.rules-get-an-end, queued in the change of the setting). Enforced by: m7_wp14_a_rule_that_never_runs_out_needs_the_setting, ARCH-SETTINGS and SEC-MATRIX.
  • Nothing waits for a person by design. With Accept by itself when its checks pass (decision 6) the loop of a rule that hands over runs with nobody watching; Accepted by itself in My agents lists those attempts until a person has looked at them. Questions and plans that need approval still wait, as the agent or the hand-over asks. Enforced by: m7_wp14_an_accept_by_itself_of_a_hand_over_of_a_rule_is_listed_in_my_agents.

Amendment (M7, WP-15): agents have a switch of their own

agents.enabled is the switch of agents for the organization and for each project, as before, and it is now the only switch that decides about agents: the switch of the assistant (ai.enabled) no longer shuts agents out of a project, and the switch of AI apps does not either. Never sent to AI still keeps agents out. The project chain is read by the one rule of ADR-0013 (amendment WP-15). The project settings and the guide name agents first among the three kinds.

Consequences

  • One new kind of actor in bb-policy (agent), evaluated as the intersection of its person's rights, its work and its limits. The access-key narrowing of ADR-0025, decision 8, is reused for agent keys.
  • New records: agents, hand-overs, standing rules, agent work with attempts, questions and reviews. Runs reuse change_run.
  • New words in the glossary (Agent, Hand over, Brief, Done when, Standing rule, Agent work, Attempt, the agent states, Accept / Send back / Throw away, My agents, Agent key, Written by an AI app / an agent); Bot account gives way to Agent, and the assistant's entry no longer forbids the word agent.
  • M7 grows by AI-30…AI-38 and the new permission; its demo shows a hand-over, a question, a review and Throw away.
  • The UX design gains the hand-over window, agent work on the issue page, My agents and its phone form (UX concept).

Alternatives considered

  • Agents as ordinary members with roles: an agent could hold more than the person who set it up, and nobody would clearly answer for it. Rejected.
  • Assigning issues to agents: blurs who answers for the issue, and makes AI part of who-does-what decisions about people. Rejected; worked on by shows the agent instead.
  • Access by saved search only: anybody who edits an issue so that it matches gives the agent that issue, Guests included. Kept only for standing rules with narrow powers; real work goes through a hand-over by ID.
  • Agent progress as comments: buries the conversation between people under logs. Rejected; agent work is its own record with one summary comment.
  • Bugaboo running agents: needs heavy machines and access to code, and is out of scope (decision).

Amendment (M7, WP-09): what was built for decision 9

  • The tools take, report, ask, attach, submit, give_up, changes_since and propose are in the one registry. They are offered to agents only (Tool::is_for_agents); the tools of a person's own time (log_time, start_timer, stop_timer) are never offered to an agent (M7-Q7). Each tool that changes something answers a preview from the plan of the use case it runs (plan_* in agent_work), so what is shown is what would be saved. An agent that calls a tool signs in at /mcp with its key; what it changes is recorded through the channel mcp.
  • Taking is judged twice: on the work the agent reads, and again under a lock of the issue in the change that starts the attempt, so of two agents who take the same issue at the same moment one gets it. A take with the version of the issue it read is refused with what changed when the issue moved on.
  • Limits are counted in agents/limits.rs and nowhere else. A change is counted once for a request, when the key of the agent is read: the table of use cases says which inputs change something (an input that does not end in Query), and a tool that changes something says it for itself. Issues at once and attempts on one issue are judged where an attempt starts (take, the first report). Over a limit the request does not start, the agent is paused (agent.paused_for holds the limit), and its person is told through the notification An agent was stopped or paused. Resume lets the agent start again from nothing. A key counts toward its agent; the calls a key makes are counted as for every key (ADR-0042, decision 6).
  • Edit locks: an agent holds no lock of an open editor. A save of a long text by an agent takes a lock for that one save (Ctx::lock_for_one_save), never when anybody holds one, and lets go of it when the save is done or refused; a refused text of an agent is nobody's draft. Enforced by: ai_36_an_agent_never_takes_over_a_lock and ai_36_an_agent_holds_a_lock_for_one_save_and_no_longer.
  • Author marks: every text of an answer is fenced with the kind of its author: the note of the brief and the answers are the word of a person (someone in the project, a Guest, someone outside), what the agent wrote is the word of an agent, and a change in changes since carries the kind of whoever wrote what is new in it.
  • Standing rules reach an agent through changes_since (the issues that came under its rules since the mark) and propose, which saves a proposal on the issue and nothing else.

Amendment (M9): agents may wait, hand over and undo, when their person allows it

The maintainer decided on 2026-11-19 that people must be able to do with their agents what they need, also where the model above forbids it. An outside test with several agents hit three walls: an agent could not wait for work, could not hand work to another agent, and could not undo what it did, so what it wrote and could not take back ended up in what the next agent read. What it changes (WP-16 of M9):

  • Decision 3, "two ways, and no third". There are still two ways to give an agent work, a hand-over and a standing rule. A hand-over is now made by a person, by a rule that hands over, or by another agent of the same person whose person switched on May hand over to my other agents (off when the agent is made). It is the same hand-over through the same use case (hand_over, plan_hand_over, HandOverPlan::record_change), with the person's rights checked as for the person's own hand-over, and the same limits, budget and end. The agent hands over only issues of its own open work, only to another agent of its person and never to itself, and gives at most what its own hand-over of that issue gives it: no power or field it lacks, a plan that waits for approval when its own does, no acceptance by itself where its own has none, each budget at most its own, and an end no later than its own. The event has the agent as its actor, and the hand-over keeps by_agent. A chain is capped: a person's hand-over is depth 0, an agent's is one deeper than its own hand-over of that issue, and depth 3 is the most (MOST_HAND_OVER_DEPTH); with one open hand-over of an issue per agent, this rules out loops. Enforced by: ai_31_an_agent_hands_over_only_when_its_switch_is_on, ai_31_an_agent_hands_over_only_issues_of_its_own_work_and_gives_no_more_than_it_has, ai_31_a_chain_of_hand_overs_stops_at_its_depth, SEC-MATRIX (the tool hand_over_work).
  • Decision 6, the review (E9, AI-35), and decision 7, runs. A person still reviews every result; Accept, Send back and Throw away are unchanged in who may give them. Two things are added.
