The check of a receiver (decision 4) is Ctx::canonical_text: the text is read and checked with the fields the person may read everywhere (Ctx::looked_in, the read that looked_at of a search has, taken from the tree and the levels read once for the request; ADR-0005 amendment M5), and the columns and the grouping must be readable fields (the Issue ID column, the word id, is the one word that is no field; it is reserved, so no own field takes it and a field named Id is refused with name.taken). Every name in the text (people, groups, member of, projects, Issue IDs, statuses, types, choices, tags, labels) is resolved by Ctx::search_names, the one function that runs a search and checks a saved one (ADR-0005 item 9): a text that names something the person cannot know (names_unknown) does not check, so a person who is shown people by their role only cannot use a saved search that names one, and an Issue ID names an issue the person reads. The same function makes the canonical text when a search is saved or changed, and a text that does not check for its maker is request.invalid. A list of shared searches skips the ones that fail and goes on within the bound of item 4, so a page that is short because searches were skipped tells nothing, but see the end of this item for one that ends at the bound of names. What resolving names reads depends on what a text names: a search that does not exist, one that does not reach the person and one that fails the check of its fields run the same reads, and only a search that a share reaches, that passes the check of its fields and fails on a name costs the reads of that name, accepted because the person could tell, by time or by a page of Shared with me that ends at the bound of names (a short page with the last search shown as its cursor, followed by an empty page), that a search shared with them exists and fails on some name, which the person who shared it chose to tell them (12-security.md, the row of saved searches; proof sec_06_a_hidden_saved_search_and_a_missing_one_run_the_same_reads). A request resolves each name once, and at most NAME_RESOLUTIONS_MAX (200) names with a read each (people and Issue IDs; the groups, tags and labels are read once as a whole). A name past the bound is never answered as unknown: the page of the list ends before that search and the next page starts after the last search shown, with a budget of its own, so every search that checks cleanly is in the list; a page with no search yet goes on to the first one it can show, at most LOOKED_AT_MAX searches looked at. The cost of a request is bounded by these two numbers; this was accepted.
  9. At most 500 saved searches per person (trash included, limit.reached) and at most 100 shares of one search, counted in the change that writes, under an advisory lock of the maker (LockClass::SavedSearches) on PostgreSQL, so two requests at the same moment cannot pass the limits.

Enforced by (additional): the tests qry_06_* of bb-core, bb-app, bb-store and bb-server.

Amendment: Spacing is the person's own

The maintainer decided after M5 that Spacing (Comfortable or Compact) is a personal choice of how Bugaboo looks, not a part of a list. Before, it stood in three places: My settings › Appearance, the controls above the list next to Group by, and the phone's Filters sheet (M5 exit decision D2), and a saved search kept it. Decided:

  1. Spacing is a setting of the person only: My settings › Appearance › Spacing (appearance.spacing, which an organization may still set and lock). Every screen follows it, the list and a saved search included. Neither the controls above the list nor the Filters sheet of a phone has Spacing.
  2. What a saved search keeps (decision 1) is the kind of view, the columns with their order and widths, and the grouping. The built-in list (decision 6) is the columns of UX design §4.2, grouped by status, at the person's Spacing.
  3. The address of a list carries the text, show, cols, widths, group and open, and no spacing. An address written before, which still says spacing=…, opens as usual: the part is not read, and it is gone the next time the list writes its address (a change of the text, the columns or the grouping).
  4. The stored field goes: migration 30 takes saved_search.spacing away (ALTER TABLE … DROP COLUMN, the same statement on SQLite and PostgreSQL, the way migration 20 took mention.read_at away). The API's PresentationRef has no spacing any more. Saved searches came after the API freeze (m4-done), so the frozen copy does not hold them and ARCH-API-FREEZE allows the change; a client that still sends spacing in a body is not refused, the member is not read. A search saved before opens with everything else it kept. The history of a search keeps the spacing its old events named; it is not rewritten.

Enforced by (additional): the tests qry_06_migration_30_* of bb-store (both databases), the API test of saving a search with an old body (bb-server), the unit tests of the list view and the address, and the browser test that the list follows Spacing (issue-list-keep.spec.ts).

Enforced by

SEC-MATRIX (the search entry point, with saved searches), ARCH-PERMS (Share searches), ARCH-EVENTS, DATA-MARKS, PERF-N1 (the list of saved searches), and the tests of M5 WP-06 named in the security chapter.

ADR-0035: Time on issues and working hours

Status: Accepted · 2026-10-31 · refines TIME-01, TIME-02, TIME-03, TIME-04, TIME-08, TIME-09, TIME-10, TIME-12, TIME-13, PRIV-09, ADR-0006, ADR-0015, ADR-0022 and ADR-0025; decisions M6-Q3…Q11

Context

M6 lets people record two things about their time. The first is what they spent it on: a timer or a typed length on an issue, with Activity and Cost center for accounting (TIME-01, TIME-02, TIME-13). The second is when they worked: the start, the end and the breaks of each day, which German law asks every employer to record (TIME-08; the Federal Labour Court's ruling of 2022), checked against the working-time rules (TIME-09) and kept as a record that can be trusted (TIME-10).

Both are about employees, so they meet the rules that exist already: working time is sensitive employee data (PRIV-09), nothing scores or ranks people (COMP-10, ADR-0013), people are shown only as Who sees people allows (PRIV-12, ADR-0022), and a total never tells about something the reader cannot see (PRIV-13). Every stored field is marked employee_time (ADR-0015). Usual work days, away times and public holidays for planning are something else and come in M8 (ADR-0030); M6 neither reads nor writes them.

The maintainer answered M6-Q3 to M6-Q11 by taking every recommendation of the M6 plan. This record writes those answers down, so the packages that build the server and the screens read one source.

Decision

Two records, kept apart on purpose. A time entry says what time was spent on, for accounting: a person, an issue, a date, a length, a note and the fields of accounting. A work day says when a person worked, for the law: a start, an end, breaks and the person's time zone. They live in two modules (bb-app::time and bb-app::working_hours, each with its own tables) and never derive one from the other: a timer does not start a work day by itself, and a work day books no time on an issue. The timesheet shows both and compares them (Booked on issues, Working hours not booked on issues), and that comparison is the only place where they meet. Enforced by: review: a reviewer of the two server packages checks that neither module writes the other's tables or makes a record from the other's, and that the comparison reads time spent only through TimeSpentStore (decision 4).

1. Time entries, Activity, Cost center and Billable (M6-Q3, M6-Q7)

  • A time entry holds its person, its issue, its date, its length in whole minutes (1 to TIME_ENTRY_MINUTES_MAX, 1,440; the constant is defined once in bb_core::time, where the one reader of typed lengths refuses more than it, and bb-app::time reuses it), an optional note (plain text, at most TIME_NOTE_CHARS_MAX, 2,000 characters, shown as text and never as HTML), Billable and the values of its own fields in field_value (ADR-0006). It has a version, and every change is a command with its event (ARCH-EVENTS, ARCH-VERSIONED).
  • Its start. An entry saved from a timer (by Stop or Switch issue) also stores its start, the moment the timer started, and its date is the person's day of that start (decision 5). An entry made with Add time has a typed date and no start.
  • Limits. A person makes at most TIME_ENTRIES_PER_DAY_MAX (200) time entries a day. The other constants of decisions 1 and 3 are defined once in bb-app::time (WP-05) with their messages. Enforced by: review (a reviewer checks that the routes use the named constants and nothing else), backed by the tests of WP-05.
  • The length is read and written once. A typed length (1:30, 1.5, 90m) is read by the one reader of bb_core::time, and a length is written by the one writer of the wording (ADR-0033, amendment M6). Enforced by: TXT-DATES on screens, and review: no second reader of typed lengths exists.
  • Activity and Cost center are starter fields: own fields of time entries that Bugaboo makes at the first start and on the upgrade of an existing server, like the starting workflow. Administrators rename, change or remove them like any own field (CF-08). They are not built-in fields: they leave the field catalogue of bb-core.
    • Bugaboo finds each by a stable mark on the field (its starter key, activity or cost-center), never by its name, so a renamed Activity still fills the Stop timer window (the lesson of M5-F43). Enforced by: review (no code compares the name of a field with a word), backed by the test time_13_activity_and_cost_center_are_found_by_their_mark_after_a_rename of WP-05.
    • Activity is a Pick one list with Development, Testing, Documentation, Meetings, Support. Cost center is a Pick one list whose choices have a number and a name (4100 Product development), sorted by the number; it starts empty.
    • The default of an entry is the value on its issue, then on its project, then on the projects above (the nearest wins). Neither field is required at the start; an administrator can make either required, and an entry without a required value is refused with a sentence that names the field.
    • Where an issue's default is set. In the details of the issue, in a group of its own under Defaults for time booked on this issue, with the levels of the fields; a project sets its own default in its settings. The fields of time entries are no fields of the issue: the new-issue form and the layouts (of the issue page and of the new-issue form) never place them, and the layout editor does not offer them (Held::OfItsKind in bb-app). The API may still set an issue's default for booked time in the body of POST /projects/{p}/issues: the issue holds the value either way, and the decision is about what the forms ask for, not about what an issue can hold. Enforced by: the test time_13_the_default_of_an_issue_is_no_field_of_its_forms_and_stays_changeable_there and the browser tests of the new-issue form and the issue details.
  • Billable ("time that can be charged to a customer") is a yes-or-no on a time entry. Whether it is offered is an organization setting, off at the start; an administrator switches it on in Organization settings › Work › Working hours, and only then do the Stop timer window, Add time and the timesheet show the box. Switching it off hides the box and keeps the values stored.

2. Who books time: Book time (M6-Q4)

  • A new project permission, Book time: book one's own time on an issue one can see. The starting roles from Contributor up have it; Viewer and Guest do not. Its row in the catalogue (topic Time, kind, starting values) is in ADR-0025, amendment M6.
  • It also covers changing and deleting one's own entries. The timer itself is the person's own (own-account): an access key reads it, and a key that holds any permission that changes something may stop, switch, move or throw away its owner's timer, the same rule as for My settings (Actor::may_change_own); Book time is still judged on every issue whose time is saved. Nobody changes or deletes another person's entries in M6; that is TIME-06 (1.0).
  • Enforced by: ARCH-PERMS (every route of time declares it or own-account), SEC-MATRIX (the routes of the timer and of time entries for every starting role).

3. The timer (M6-Q5)

  • One running timer per person, kept on the server. Every device shows the same timer, and closing the browser does not stop it. The store holds at most one timer for a person (a unique key on the person), so two devices that start at once get one timer and one refusal with the conflict. Enforced by: TEST-CONCURRENT ("Timers and working hours start and stop at the same time", architecture §11), backed by the test time_01_one_person_has_one_running_timer_on_every_device of WP-05.
  • What a person does with it: Start (on an issue the person can see and book on), Stop, Switch issue, Change start time and Throw away (saves nothing). A person starts or switches at most TIMER_CHANGES_PER_SECOND (1) times a second.
  • Change start time takes a moment that is never in the future and never before the end of the person's last time entry that has a start (decision 1). Entries made with Add time have no start and do not bound it.
  • Switch issue is starting a timer on another issue while one runs: the time so far is saved as a time entry with the defaults of its issue, without a window, and the new timer starts. Two cases differ:
    • when a field that is required (Activity, Cost center or another own field) has no default on that issue, Switch issue opens the Stop timer window for the running entry instead of saving it silently, and the new timer starts when that entry is saved; when the person closes the window without saving, the old timer keeps running and no new one starts;
    • when the timer ran for less than a minute, nothing is saved, the new timer starts, and the person is told in one sentence ("Less than a minute on WEB-142, so no time was saved.").
  • Stop opens the Stop timer window: the note, Activity and Cost center filled in from the issue, and Billable while it is on.
  • Whole minutes. A timer is saved as whole minutes, rounded down. Under one minute nothing is saved, and the window says so.
  • A timer longer than one entry can be. When a timer has run longer than TIME_ENTRY_MINUTES_MAX (1,440 minutes), Stop timer asks the person to change the start time first and saves nothing until the length fits; Bugaboo never cuts the time by itself.
  • The long-timer warning. A timer that runs longer than the longest day of the organization's working-time rules (10 hours in the preset Germany, and 10 hours with No rules) shows a warning on the timer and sends the person one notification, by the job timers.long-running (how it is queued and when it does nothing: ADR-0017, amendment M6).
  • The work day and the timer stay two records: starting a timer while the work day has not started asks "Start your work day too?", and End work day while a timer runs asks "Stop the timer on WEB-142 too?". Neither starts or ends anything without the person's answer.

4. Estimated time, Time left, totals and the port of time spent (M6-Q6)

  • Estimated time and Time left are lengths in minutes stored on the issue and changed like any field (a version, an event, the history, field levels). Time spent is the total of the issue's time entries; it is read, never typed.

  • The worked-out Time left. While nobody has typed Time left, it is Estimated time minus Time spent, never below zero, and the screens show it in the quiet style of a value worked out. A typed value counts until it is cleared. It is worked out in one place, in bb-core. The worked-out Time left follows the permission of Time left alone: a reader who may read it sees it, also without the right to read Time spent, and what a reader can work out from fields they may read is the administrator's choice, which Bugaboo does not second-guess (a decision of the maintainer).

  • Totals. An issue shows its own numbers and, when it has sub-issues, the totals with them (every level below). A project shows the totals of its issues and its sub-projects.

  • A total counts only what the reader may see: only the issues the reader sees and only the fields the reader may read, by the same compiled search that gives the list (ADR-0004), so a total never tells about a hidden issue or a hidden field (PRIV-13). Enforced by: SEC-MATRIX (the totals under each starting role), ARCH-DB-PARITY (the same totals on both databases).

  • One definition of time spent in SQL. The minutes spent on an issue (the sum of the lengths of its time entries) are written once, as one expression of the search compiler in bb-store (search/), which the field Time spent of the search language uses. spent_on_issues and spent_on_search of the port below reuse that expression and write no second sum. Enforced by: ARCH-DB-PARITY (the same numbers on both databases), and review: a second sum of time entries anywhere in bb-store is a finding.

  • The worked-out Time left in a search (to filter, sort or show it as a column) is one SQL expression of the compiler too. It is the second place of the rule of bb-core, so it is held to it like the approved pair of ADR-0033 (coding-standards §1): cargo xtask gen time-vectors writes tools/testdata/time-left.json from bb-core (estimate, time spent, a typed value or none, and the answer), DOC-GENERATED fails when the file differs from the code, and the test time_03_the_compiled_time_left_matches_the_vectors runs every case through the compiler on both databases. WP-07 adds the generator and the test.

  • The port of time spent, TimeSpentStore, in crates/bb-app/src/time/spent.rs, is how everything outside the module of time entries reads time spent. WP-05 implements it in bb-store; the totals (WP-07) and the timesheet's comparison with working hours (WP-06, WP-10) read it, and their tests use a fake of it until the store has it. Its shape:

    /// The minutes booked on issues, for the readers outside the module of time entries.
pub trait TimeSpentStore: ChangeStore + 'static {
    /// The minutes booked on each issue of `issues`, one row for each, `Minutes(0)` for an
    /// issue without entries. Reads only the issues in the list.
    fn spent_on_issues(
        &self,
        issues: &[IssueId],
    ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Vec<(IssueId, Minutes)>, Self::Error>> + Send;

    /// The sum of the minutes booked on the issues that `request` finds: the compiled search
    /// of the list, with the reader's sight and fields in it, in one statement. Like
    /// `search_count`, it ignores `after` and `limit`.
    fn spent_on_search(
        &self,
        request: &SearchRequest,
    ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Minutes, SearchFailure>> + Send;

    /// The minutes `person` booked on each date from `first` to `last` (both included), by
    /// the date of each entry; a date without entries is left out.
    fn booked_per_date(
        &self,
        person: UserId,
        first: Date,
        last: Date,
    ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Vec<(Date, Minutes)>, Self::Error>> + Send;
}

    Minutes is the whole minutes of bb_core::time (the type of lengths, coding-standards §3), Date is jiff::civil::Date, and SearchRequest and SearchFailure are those of bb-app::search. SearchRequest.me is only what me means in the search text, never the reader whose rights count: those are in sight and fields.

  • The port decides nothing. It never reads an issue the caller did not pass: spent_on_issues reads the rows of the listed issues and no other, spent_on_search reads the issues the compiled search finds, whose visibility predicates the use case put into the request, and booked_per_date reads one person's own entries. Which issues a reader may see, whether they may read Time spent, and whose dates they may read are decided by the use case with the policy engine before it calls the port. booked_per_date is called for the person themselves only: Working hours of others shows no time on issues in M6 (decision 8). Enforced by: ARCH-AUTHZ-ONLY (only the use case turns what the port answers into an answer), SEC-MATRIX (the totals), and review: the port's methods take no person who reads.

5. Work days and the person's day (M6-Q9)

  • A work day holds its person, its date, its periods of work (each a start and an end, none while it runs; the first start is the start of the day), its breaks (each with a start and an end), its time zone, the warnings of the working-time rules (decision 6) and a version. All moments are stored in UTC (architecture §7, Time). From the first start to the last end a work day lasts at most WORK_DAY_HOURS_MAX (24 hours), a constant that WP-06 defines once in bb-app::working_hours.
  • Periods and breaks. The time between two periods of a day is a break: the Breaks value of a day is its breaks plus those gaps, and a gap counts for the rules only in parts of at least the shortest break that counts, like any break (15 minutes in the preset Germany; the number is a rule of decision 6, a setting of the registry, and is written nowhere else). The screens show a day as its first start, its last end and its Breaks; they have no word for a period.
  • The person's day. The date of a moment for a person is the date it falls on in the person's time zone (bb_core::time, the one answer; across the changes of daylight-saving time a day has 23 or 25 hours). A work day belongs to the date it starts on in the person's zone and may end the next morning; it keeps the zone it started in, so moving to another zone later never moves a past day. A time entry's date is the person's day of its start. Enforced by: TEST-WORKING-TIME (day boundaries, daylight-saving changes, zones, a day that ends after midnight).
  • Start work day, Start break, End break and End work day record the moment of the tap; the timesheet's Work day rows take the same values typed afterwards.
  • A day left open stays open. A work day that was never ended is not ended by Bugaboo: the record has to show what really happened (TIME-10). The next Start work day first asks "When did your work day on Thursday end?", and the answer is a change of a past day (decision 7). Enforced by: TEST-WORKING-TIME (no job and no use case ends a day without the person's answer).
  • One work day per person and date. The store holds at most one work day for a person and a date (a unique key). A second Start work day on the same date after End work day reopens that day with a new period on it; it never makes a second day. Two days of one person never overlap, and a break lies inside its day. Two devices that start a day at once get one work day and one refusal with the conflict. Changes of work days are limited for each person by a named constant that WP-06 defines in bb-app::working_hours. Enforced by: TEST-CONCURRENT, ARCH-VERSIONED, TEST-WORKING-TIME (the second start on a date reopens the day).

6. The working-time rules as data (M6-Q8)

  • Rules are data, never code. The organization has one set of rules, made from a preset and stored as settings in the registry (ADR-0018): a number for each rule, which administrators may change. M6 has two presets:
    • Germany (ArbZG): at most 10 hours of work a day (§3); a break of 30 minutes after 6 hours of work and of 45 minutes after 9 hours (§4); a break counts only in parts of at least 15 minutes, and nobody works more than 6 hours in a row without such a part (§4, the two details of M6-Q8); at least 11 hours of rest between the end of one work day and the start of the next (§5).
    • No rules: nothing is checked, and the long-timer warning uses 10 hours.
  • Sundays, public holidays and the average over six months are not checked in M6 (public holidays come with M8, ADR-0030).
  • Checked after every change, never a block. After every change of a work day the rules are checked for that day and for the days next to it (the rest between two days crosses midnight), with the rules in force at that change. A broken rule becomes a warning stored with the day (which rule, and the numbers that broke it), shown in plain sentences on the timesheet. Recording is never refused because of a rule, because the record has to show what really happened (TIME-09). A later change of the rules does not rewrite the warnings of days nobody changed. Enforced by: TEST-WORKING-TIME (the unit and property tests of every rule of the preset Germany, rest across days included).
  • The rules are worked out in one pure place, bb_core::working_time, from the moments and the zone of the days; the store and the screens hold no copy of them (bb-core does no I/O, ARCH-PURE).

7. Past days, reasons and the keep period (M6-Q9, M6-Q11)

  • When a change needs a reason. A reason in the person's own words (plain text, at most REASON_CHARS_MAX, 500 characters, a constant that WP-06 defines once in bb-app::working_hours) is asked for, and the change is refused without one:
    • for any change of another person's work day, past or today;
    • for a change of one's own past day. A day is past from the next day on, in the zone of the day. A change is a new or changed start, end, period or break, or the end of a day left open.
  • The old value is kept. The event of the change carries the old values and the reason, and the history of the day shows both.
  • The person is told. When somebody else changes a person's day, the person gets a notification in the app, and by e-mail if they keep that on (ADR-0033). The notification names who changed what, with the reason, and goes to that person only.
  • Enforced by: ARCH-EVENTS (every change of a work day writes its event), TEST-WORKING-TIME (a change of another person's day, or of one's own past day, without a reason is refused; a change by somebody else notifies the person).
  • The keep period is a minimum. Work days, their breaks and the reasons of their changes are kept at least a number of whole years from their date, an organization setting. The preset Germany keeps them 2 years (ArbZG §16 (2)); with that preset the number cannot be set below 2 years. Before the keep period ends, nobody deletes a work day. This is the one place of that rule; the other documents name it as "the keep period (ADR-0035, decision 7)". Enforced by: the use case of settings (bb_core::working_time::leaves_keep_period_short is asked at every change and every reset of the preset and of the keep period, and refuses with working-hours.keep-years-too-short; the cut of the number when it is read stays only as a safety net for numbers stored before), tests time_10_the_keep_period_cannot_go_below_two_years_with_the_germany_preset and time_10_choosing_or_resetting_germany_cannot_bring_back_a_short_keep_period, SEC-MATRIX (no route deletes a younger day).
  • Nothing is deleted by itself (a decision of the maintainer). After the keep period a work day stays until an administrator deletes it. Organization settings › Work › Working hours shows how many work days are older than the keep period, for each person and in total, counted when the page is read (no job counts them), and offers Delete them, for all of them at once or for one person, with a confirmation in the page. It needs Change organization settings (ADR-0025, the permission of the Administrator role; HR does not hold it, and no access key does). Every deletion is written to the security log with how many days of whom were deleted. Deleting a day deletes its breaks and the events of its changes too, so the old values and the reasons do not outlive the day (events follow the keep-and-delete rules, ADR-0007). Enforced by: ARCH-PERMS, SEC-MATRIX (the route that deletes old work days, for every starting role), ARCH-EVENTS, and the test priv_09_old_working_hours_are_deleted_only_when_an_administrator_says_so of WP-06.
  • The organization stays responsible. Under the GDPR (storage limitation, Art. 5(1)(e)) the organization deletes what it no longer needs; whether a work day older than the keep period is still needed is the organization's judgement, not Bugaboo's. Bugaboo shows what is past the keep period and makes deleting it one step.
  • Time entries keep no rule of their own in M6. Their 10 years come with the table of Keep and delete rules (PRIV-05, M9).
  • Remove a person (PRIV-04, M9) keeps the person's work days at least for the keep period, because the law asks for them (architecture §7, Legal holds), and the work days keep the person's name, so an inspection under ArbZG §17 can tie them to the employee (a decision of the maintainer). The name is shown only to holders of See working hours of others, on Working hours of others, as decision 8 allows (Totals only included); everything else of the removed person shows Former user, as ADR-0022 says. This is the one place of that rule. Enforced by: ARCH-PERSON-REF (the name comes only through PersonRef for that place), SEC-MATRIX (a removed person's work days for every starting role).

8. Who sees working hours (M6-Q10)

  • One's own, always. Every person sees and records their own working hours and time entries.
  • Others only with a permission. Two new organization permissions: See working hours of others and Change working hours of others. A new starting role, HR, holds both; nobody has it at the start, the Administrator role does not include either, and an administrator gives HR to a group (for example Payroll). The rows in the catalogue, the role, and how a person who decides roles for the whole organization gives it, are in ADR-0025, amendment M6.
  • Working hours of others is the one place that shows another person's working hours: a person picker, then that person's week in the timesheet's work-day rows, read only, or with Change for a holder of Change working hours of others (every change with a reason, decision 7), both as Totals only allows (below). It shows no time on issues.
  • Names on that page. A holder of See working hours of others sees the names of the people whose hours they may see there, whatever Who sees people says elsewhere, like the people who manage see names in Organization settings (ADR-0025, decision 11; ADR-0022, amendment M6). The page's answers carry each person as PersonRef, which bb-policy resolves for this place to Names when the reader holds the permission; no raw person data leaves the use case. Enforced by: ARCH-PERSON-REF.
  • Totals only (an organization setting, off at the start): while it is on, Working hours of others shows each person's total of the week and nothing else (no days, no starts, ends or breaks, no warnings), for every reader, holders of See working hours of others and of Change working hours of others alike. Because a change needs the day, Totals only turns changes of other people's days off while it is on: a holder of Change working hours of others reads the totals and changes nothing. The team reports of 1.0 obey it too. This is the one place of that rule; the other documents point to "ADR-0035, decision 8".
  • Time entries of others. A list of another person's time entries waits for TIME-06 (1.0); on an issue, the entries of others show as Who sees people allows.
  • HR's starting levels, like every starting role's (ADR-0025, decision 4): every field Hidden and every kind of people information Hidden, because HR gives no work in projects; a person who also holds another role gets that role's levels, the most open one counting. The generated tables of architecture §7 show HR when WP-06 adds it to the definition in bb-policy.
  • Nowhere else. No other page, total, count, history, notification, e-mail, export or search tells a person about another's working hours. A time entry of another person shows only as Who sees people and the field levels allow (the kind Time entries; Time spent as a field). Enforced by: SEC-MATRIX (the routes of work days and of Working hours of others for every starting role, HR included, and with Totals only on), ARCH-PERSON-REF.
  • Every gift and every removal of these two permissions, and every change of the working-time settings (the preset, a rule, the keep period, Totals only, Billable), is written to the security log (PRIV-09: "changes to these settings are recorded"). Enforced by: ARCH-EVENTS, and the generated test sec_15_every_change_of_permissions_is_in_the_security_log of ADR-0025, decision 9, which covers the new permissions.

9. No scores, no rankings, no AI

  • No route, export, search or list orders, ranks or compares people by a number of time: not by working hours, not by time booked, not by warnings, not by Time spent. A list of people is in the order of their names, and a total of a person is shown for that person alone. Grouping by person in the search language never gives a length per person.
  • No AI tool reads working hours. The tool registry has no tool that reads work days, breaks, warnings or the totals of a person, and none that reads another person's time entries (ADR-0013, COMP-10).
  • No time entry by an agent (M7-Q7). An agent never makes a time entry and never starts a timer; the time and cost it reports stay on its attempt, marked as reported by the agent, and no total of Time spent counts them (ADR-0029, decision 4). An AI app acting for a person books only that person's own time, with the person's Book time.
  • Enforced by: SEC-MATRIX (no route of time takes an order by person or by a total), ARCH-AI-TOOLS (no tool reaches the use cases of working hours), the tests priv_09_… of WP-05 and WP-06, and ai_33_an_agent_never_makes_a_time_entry (M7).

Amendment (WP-05): Activity and Cost center leave the catalogue, the API keeps their words

Activity and Cost center are own fields of time entries (decision 1), so the values Activity and CostCenter of the built-in Field of bb-core are gone, with their starting levels and their rows in the generated field table. The API was frozen with the words activity and cost-center in the schema Field (ADR-0008, amendment M4), and API v1 does not take a word away: the schema keeps them, marked retired (bb_core::fields::RETIRED_FIELD_WORDS). A request that names one is accepted and nothing happens (a level of the field is not set, a layout places nothing, a rule of a workflow asks for nothing); no answer names them, because no field of the catalogue is either. The mapping is at the edge of the API only (bb_api::api::is_retired_field); no frozen copy is written again. Enforced by: ARCH-API-FREEZE (the schema still holds both words), and the test of bb-core that no field of the catalogue has a retired word.

An upgraded server holds the two words where the program no longer reads them: a role that was reset or copied has a level for every field of the old catalogue, and a layout may place Cost center. Migration 31 deletes the levels of the two fields that roles and projects set, plain and for one issue type, and their places in layouts (the fields, the fields taken off a form, and their roles), so reading the rights or a layout never meets an unknown word. A rule of a workflow never held them: a rule may name only the description, the people an issue is assigned to and own fields (rule_may_name, since workflows exist). Enforced by: the upgrade test of migration 31 on both databases.

The values of the own fields of time entries are kept in a table of their own, time_entry_value, with the columns of field_value and every part marked employee_time, basis contract (ADR-0015), instead of the shared field_value, whose marks are those of issues and projects. The rows of the domain events and of the history about a time entry or a timer are marked the same way by the kind of their record (#[personal_for(kind = …)], ADR-0015): their changes, and their moment, which there is when a person started or stopped work. The table shares the column names of field_value (one enum, FieldValueRow, named in brackets in stored_tables!). Enforced by: DATA-MARKS.

Amendment (M8): the totals read the three lengths in one statement

The totals of a search (an issue with its sub-issues, a project) read Time spent in the same statement as the sums of Estimated time and Time left, search_lengths of the search port, which now answers all three (LengthTotals::time_spent), each only for a field among the readable ones of the request, as before. spent_on_search leaves the port of time spent, which nothing else read; the port keeps spent_on_issues and booked_per_date, and the issue's own time and the timesheet read time spent through it as before. The reason is speed: the large dataset of M8 gives estimates to a share of the biggest project, so the worked-out Time left reads each of those issues from the table, and the time spent read every issue of the project from the table a second time; one statement reads each issue once (the benchmark project-time-totals, architecture §11, M6-F186). Nothing about what a total counts changes: the same compiled search with the reader's sight and fields, and the one expression of the minutes spent on an issue (decision 4), now summed for each issue found instead of over the entries joined to them. The worked-out Time left reads the minutes spent once for an issue, as the larger of the difference and zero. Enforced by: ARCH-DB-PARITY (time_03_the_totals_add_the_time_left_and_the_time_spent_of_every_level and the parity tests of time spent, on both databases), the vectors of time_03_the_compiled_time_left_matches_the_vectors, and SEC-MATRIX (the totals under each starting role).

Consequences

  • New tables for timers, time entries, work days and breaks, each column with its personal-data mark (DATA-MARKS); the values of own fields of time entries in time_entry_value. Every column that says something about a person's time is employee_time (architecture §12, Personal data in M6).
  • New permissions in the catalogue (Book time, See working hours of others, Change working hours of others), a new topic Time and a new starting role HR (ADR-0025, amendment M6).
  • New settings in the registry: the preset and each number of the working-time rules, the keep period, Totals only and Billable, all on Organization settings › Work › Working hours (UX §5.1).
  • One new kind of job, timers.long-running (ADR-0017, amendment M6), two new notification kinds (a long timer; a day changed by somebody else), two new checks, TEST-WORKING-TIME and TXT-DATES, and a generated file of vectors for the worked-out Time left (tools/testdata/time-left.json, decision 4), the second approved pair of coding-standards §1.
  • Activity and Cost center leave the field catalogue of bb-core, so the generated table of fields in architecture §7 loses their rows when WP-05 builds them as starter fields.

Alternatives considered

  • One record for both (time entries carry the start and end of the day): a person who books two hours on an issue has not said when they worked, and a day's working hours are not the sum of what was booked on issues. The law asks for the second, accounting for the first. Rejected.
  • Ending a day left open by itself at midnight or after 10 hours: the record would show something that did not happen. Rejected (TIME-10).
  • Refusing a day that breaks a rule: a person who worked 11 hours could not record it, and the record would lie. Rejected (TIME-09).
  • Giving See working hours of others to the Administrator role: the people who set up the server would see everybody's working hours without anyone deciding it. Rejected; an administrator gives HR on purpose, and the security log records it.
  • A timer that lives in the browser: two devices would run two timers, and a closed browser would lose the time. Rejected (TIME-01).
  • Activity and Cost center as built-in fields: an organization could not rename or remove them (TIME-13). Rejected.

Enforced by

TEST-WORKING-TIME, TXT-DATES, TEST-CONCURRENT, SEC-MATRIX, ARCH-PERMS, ARCH-PERSON-REF, ARCH-AUTHZ-ONLY, ARCH-AI-TOOLS, ARCH-EVENTS, ARCH-VERSIONED, ARCH-SETTINGS, ARCH-PURE, ARCH-DB-PARITY and DATA-MARKS (see tools/checks/catalog.toml), backed by the named tests of WP-05, WP-06 and WP-07, and review where the decisions say so.

Amendment (M9): old work days are the first user of the use case of old records

The count of old work days and Delete them (decision 7) are the use cases old_records and delete_old_records of bb_app::keeping, for the kind work-days of KEEP_KINDS (ADR-0045, decision 6). Time entries are the second kind: kept at least keeping.time-entry-years (10 at the start) from their day, then counted and deleted the same way, with the values of their fields and the events and history rows that carry their note (M6-F45), and the security-log action time_entries.deleted. The routes /api/v1/work-days/old stay at their addresses and answer as before; the general routes are below /api/v1/admin/keep-rules.

Amendment: Add time takes a day in the future

Add time on an issue (the screen, the API and the tool log_time) takes any day, a day in the future too: a person who books planned time ahead, such as a workshop next week that a customer has already ordered, books it on the day it will happen. The rest of decision 1 holds for such an entry: its length, its limit per day and its fields, and it counts in Time spent from the moment it is saved. The other records of time still never reach into the future: the timer starts now and Change start time never moves its start past now (decision 3, timer.start-in-the-future), and a work day, its periods and its breaks are never in the future (decision 5, working-hours.in-the-future), because they record what happened and when. The maintainer decided this. Enforced by: the test time_02_add_time_and_log_time_take_a_day_in_the_future (bb-app), which books the next day with Add time and with log_time, and the tests of the timer and of work days that refuse the future.

ADR-0036: License: AGPL-3.0-or-later, other terms from the maintainer, a contributor agreement

Status: Accepted · 2026-10-31

Context

Bugaboo is about to be published. The license of the code was open (the feature list said "decide later"). What is wanted:

  • Anyone may run and change Bugaboo, also in a closed setting for their own use.
  • Whoever distributes a changed version, or offers it to others over a network, must make its source available, so the maintainer can read and merge it.
  • The maintainer can also offer Bugaboo under other terms, for example an edition with additions that are not published.

Decision

  1. The code of Bugaboo is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later (SPDX AGPL-3.0-or-later). LICENSE holds the official text. The identifier is in Cargo.toml ([workspace.package], which every crate inherits) and in every package.json of the project.
  2. The maintainer offers Bugaboo under other terms on request. To be able to do that for the whole code, every contribution comes with a contributor license agreement (CONTRIBUTING.md): contributors keep their copyright and grant the maintainer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to use, sublicense and relicense the contribution under any terms, plus a patent license. It is accepted in the pull request with a comment.
  3. No dependency from the GPL family (GPL, LGPL, AGPL, in any version) goes into Bugaboo: code under someone else's GPL could not be offered under other terms. The allow list in deny.toml names none of them, so cargo deny refuses them for Rust, and DEP-LICENSES refuses them for npm packages, also those that only run on a developer machine. A package that offers a choice (MIT OR GPL-3.0-only) is fine when the other side is on the allow list.
  4. Parts that third parties build on may be under the MIT license, so that using them does not carry the AGPL into other programs. The first is @bugaboo/api-client (web/packages/api-client, the generated TypeScript client of the public API): MIT, with its own LICENSE file and "license": "MIT" in its package.json. A further part (a plug-in kit, examples) gets the same treatment by an amendment of this record.
  5. Until a lawyer has reviewed the agreement, nothing commercial is offered.

Consequences

  • Every new crate or package carries the license (license.workspace = true, or "license": "AGPL-3.0-or-later" in package.json), except the MIT parts named in decision 4.
  • A change of the allow list or of the license of the project needs a new decision record.
  • A pull request is merged only after its author has accepted the agreement (review).

Alternatives considered

  • MIT or Apache-2.0 for everything: anyone could close a changed version and keep it, and the maintainer could not read or merge it. Rejected.
  • GPL-3.0: does not cover use over a network, which is how Bugaboo is run. Rejected.
  • A source-available license (BUSL, SSPL): not open source, and the allow list refuses such licenses in dependencies for the same reasons. Rejected.

Enforced by

DEP-LICENSES (the allow list has no GPL family, npm included, with cargo deny and deny.toml), review for the agreement in pull requests.

ADR-0037: No hosted CI; verification is local

Status: Accepted · 2026-11-01

Context

The repository had a workflow file for a hosted CI service, prepared for the day the code moves to a public Git host. Hosted runners cost money on private repositories, repeat what the development computer already runs, and need a second place where the commands are listed and kept in step with the first.

Decision

  • No hosted CI. There is no .github/workflows/ folder and no workflow linter (actionlint, check LINT-CI). META-WIRING no longer reads workflow files.
  • Verification is local. The pre-push hook runs the push checks (cargo xtask check push); cargo xtask ci is the full local run (checks, tests of both databases, browser build, browser tests) and runs before main moves. Nothing reaches main without it.
  • Releases are built, signed and published locally; the release page on the Git host is created by hand.
  • Hosted automation stays off on the public repository (the repository setting is switched off before the first push).

Consequences

  • One list of commands (catalog.toml) and one runner; no second description of the same steps.
  • A contributor's pull request is verified by the maintainer, who runs cargo xtask ci on it.

Alternatives considered

  • Keep the workflow, run it by hand only: a file that never runs drifts from the real commands. Rejected.
  • Run only the cheap checks in hosted CI: a partial copy of the gate, and a second place to keep current. Rejected.

Enforced by

META-WIRING (hooks call only xtask); the rest by review.

ADR-0038: Public identity and plain commit messages

Status: Accepted · 2026-11-01

Context

The history of the repository is published with it. Until now commits carried the identity Git found on the machine, the working vocabulary of the project (folder and branch names, work packages, milestone codes), session lines of the tool that wrote them, and merges in a form that named a branch and a package. None of that tells a reader of the public history what changed, and some of it is private.

Decision

  • One public identity. The maintainer's commits are authored and committed as the name of the GitHub account with its noreply address (Name <id+Name@users.noreply.github.com>). The identity is configuration, never code: the local Git configuration of the master and of every work folder, copied by cargo xtask setup (from the origin master when that is a folder, or from the variable BUGABOO_PUBLIC_IDENTITY). The handle itself may appear in files and messages only in its GitHub forms: the noreply address and github.com/<login> links.
  • What counts as public. An identity is public when its address is a GitHub noreply address whose login is its name, or when it is the identity GitHub writes for merges made on its web site. Another contributor's public identity passes as well, because it is not the maintainer's private one; a real name or a private address in the author field never passes. A contribution that arrives with another identity is brought in by the maintainer (a squash or a new commit) rather than by relaxing the rule.
  • Where it is checked. The commit-msg hook reads the author and committer about to be recorded (git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT, GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT). The push and full checks read the author and committer of every commit that is on no remote yet. Both are part of SEC-PRIVATE, with the private list (words, several words, e-mail addresses; the variable BUGABOO_PRIVATE_WORDS names another file) and the refusal of the session key of Claude Code in memory notes.
  • Plain messages in the common pattern. GIT-COMMIT-MSG enforces what coding-standards §2 ("Commits") says, in one place: Conventional Commit types, a first line in the imperative mood of at most 72 characters, a body wrapped at 72 after one blank line, no merge subject (Amendment, ADR-0041: branches are rebased, so no merge commit is made; the merge commits made before keep their Merge <what it brought> subjects), Git's own Revert "..." form, the single trailer Co-Authored-By: Claude <model> <noreply@anthropic.com>, no claude.ai link or session line, and none of the working vocabulary. The imperative is a heuristic (no determiner, no past or -ing form, no third-person form of a common verb). A good first line is fix(theme): keep a long word in an alert on its own line; a bad one is fix(theme): the list keeps its scroll position. The word list is in xtask/src/checks/git_commit_msg/jargon.rs, once.
  • Rewriting history. Commits that are on the public remote are never rewritten. History that has never been published may be rewritten once, before the first push, to bring it into line with these rules.

Consequences

  • The published history reads the same for everyone and carries no private identity.
  • Until the unpublished history is rewritten, the push and full checks report its old identities and messages.
  • A word of the working vocabulary is refused even when it is used in its ordinary sense; the message is reworded. The exceptions are the product words "project lead" (a role) and "master key" (encryption), listed with the words.

Alternatives considered

  • Hard-code the identity in the check: puts the handle into the code outside its GitHub forms. Rejected.
  • Allow any noreply address: lets another person's identity pass as the maintainer's. It is accepted only because it is public, and documented.
  • Check the identity only at commit time: a commit made with --no-verify or on another machine would reach the remote. Rejected.

Enforced by

SEC-PRIVATE (identity, private list, memory-note key) and GIT-COMMIT-MSG (message rules).

ADR-0039: Explicit master configuration; only the master publishes

Status: Accepted · 2026-11-01

Context

ADR-0024 keeps a master checkout that never builds, and recognised it by a path segment (a folder whose name starts with OneDrive). That is one person's setup, not the project's: anyone who clones into a synced folder would be locked out of building, and the master would be undetectable anywhere else. Publishing was also open: any checkout could push anywhere, and the public remote is reached from exactly one place.

Decision

  • The master is marked, never guessed. A checkout is the master only when BUGABOO_CHECKOUT_ROLE=master is set in the environment or in the ignored file .env.local at its root. cargo xtask guard-master writes it, from a work folder (the master builds nothing): the .env.local mark, a pre-push hook in .git/bugaboo-hooks/ together with core.hooksPath pointing there (so the hook runs whatever other hook folder is configured), and a program for Cargo's rustc-wrapper in .cargo/config.local.toml, so even a plain cargo build stops. Without the mark a plain clone builds, tests and commits as it is. The edit hook of Claude Code reads the same mark.
  • Only the master publishes. A work folder pushes only to a remote that is a path (the master); only the master pushes to a remote on the network (the public one): git -C <master> push github main. One tested function, publish::plan, decides from the role and the URL of the remote (a path or a network address): a work folder to a path runs the checks of a push; the master to the network runs only the checks that build nothing (SEC-PRIVATE on the commits to push and on every tracked file, GIT-LINEAR on the commits to push, DEP-LICENSES: Amendment, ADR-0041); every other combination is refused with a message that names the master command. main only moves to a commit that passed the full run in a work folder, so the master does not repeat it. main moves by a fast-forward only, and the commits it receives are a straight line (ADR-0041).
  • The master's hook uses a program built elsewhere. The hook calls the xtask program of the work folder that ran guard-master; if that program is gone, the hook says to run the command again.
  • Placeholders. Rule texts name the master as <master> and the folder of the work folders as <work root>; the concrete paths are the maintainer's own setup, kept outside the repository.

Consequences

  • No path decides anything; the old guard for OneDrive folders and the tracked Windows batch file are gone, the build-refusing program is written per master.
  • When the xtask program that the hook calls moves or is deleted, guard-master is run again.
  • ADR-0024 is amended: its guard and its hook rule now follow this record.

Alternatives considered

  • Keep detecting by path: locks out other people's setups. Rejected.
  • Publish from a work folder (the earlier flow): the public remote would be reachable from every checkout and needs the full checks repeated by the hook. Rejected.
  • A tracked hook script for the master: a second place to keep current, and a file type without a linter. The hook is written by the command instead.

Enforced by

BUILD-LOCATION (the mark is read before every build, test and install command); META-WIRING (the pre-push command of lefthook and the edit hook); the pre-push plan by its tests in xtask/src/publish.rs and xtask/src/main.rs; GIT-LINEAR (no merge commit in the commits to push, ADR-0041).

ADR-0040: Version numbers follow the plan

Status: Accepted · 2026-10-31

Context

Bugaboo is published before it is finished. Its version number should tell a reader how far it is, and it should not be chosen by feeling. The plan already measures progress: 04-milestones lists every milestone with the number of features it brings, and a finished milestone gets a tag mN-done.

Decision

  1. 0.9.0 means feature complete: every feature of the plan is built, that is every milestone up to M14. M15 (live updates and the release itself) brings 1.0.0.
  2. Before that, the minor number follows the features done: minor = floor(9 × done / total), where done counts the features of the milestones that carry their mN-done tag, and total the features of M0 to M14 (the Features column of the overview in 04-milestones). With M0 to M5 done that is floor(9 × 96 / 225) = 3: 0.3.0.
  3. The patch number counts the releases made at the same minor number, from 0. A finished milestone that does not raise the minor number raises the patch number.
  4. The version is written once, in [workspace.package] of Cargo.toml, which every crate inherits; the browser packages carry no version of their own. It changes in the commit that records a finished milestone.

Consequences

  • The number moves only when a milestone is done, so it never claims work that is not tagged.
  • A change of the plan's feature counts changes the arithmetic; the version is not lowered for that, the next milestone simply catches up.

Alternatives considered

  • The milestone number as minor (M5 → 0.5.0): the plan has more milestones than nine before 1.0, so the numbers would run out. Rejected.
  • Calendar versions: say nothing about how complete Bugaboo is. Rejected.

Enforced by

review (the arithmetic needs the plan's table and the milestone tags, which no check reads yet): checked at the commit that records a finished milestone.

ADR-0041: Branches are rebased, never merged

Status: Accepted · 2026-10-31

Context

The lead combined each builder's branch with the lead's branch WIN1 by a merge commit (Merge the search page, ADR-0038), and main moved to WIN1 by a fast-forward. The history of main therefore has a merge commit for every work package, and so will the public main. Each package appears twice in it (its own commits and the merge), and git bisect walks into the side branches. The public repository's ruleset on main can require a straight line ("Require linear history"); a merge commit would then reach GitHub only on the maintainer's bypass. The sister project made the same decision on the same day.

Decision

  • Branches are combined by rebasing. The lead makes a copy of the package branch, rebases the copy onto WIN1 (conflicts are resolved commit by commit during the rebase), and then moves WIN1 to it with git merge --ff-only. No merge commit is made, on any branch that reaches main. Enforced by: GIT-LINEAR.
  • WIN1, the master's main and the public main stay a straight line. The pre-push hook refuses a merge commit among the commits a push adds, on a work folder's push to the master and on the master's push to the public remote. The commits are chosen the same way as for the private-data guard (on a local branch, a tag or HEAD, and on no remote-tracking branch); one function chooses them for both, and the finding names the local branches that hold the merge commit. A plain clone, whose origin is no marked master, is not checked. Enforced by: GIT-LINEAR.
  • Where the check is off. It is on in the master and in a checkout whose origin is a folder this program can open and that is marked as the master (.env.local). It is off when origin is an address on the network (a plain clone), and also when origin is a path it cannot open as a folder (a Git Bash path such as /c/…, a file:// address, a path of WSL) or a folder without the mark. In the last cases it prints one line that it is off and never fails for it (review: the work folders keep origin as a plain path to the marked master, which cargo xtask guard-master writes).
  • A builder brings in a newer main by rebasing its own branch onto origin/main and pushes it again with git push --force-with-lease origin WINn. Only the builder's own WINn is ever force-pushed; WIN1, main and every branch on the public remote never are (review: which branch is pushed with force is the person's choice, not something the hook can tell).
  • The merge commits already on main stay. They were made before this decision and are already on every remote, so the check, which reads only what is on no remote, leaves them out; history is not rewritten.
  • No merge subject. A commit message never has the subject of a merge (Merge …); this replaces the Merge <what it brought> form of ADR-0038. Git's Revert "..." stays. Enforced by: GIT-COMMIT-MSG.
  • The public side: the ruleset of the public repository requires linear history on main ("Require linear history"), so GitHub refuses a merge commit as well. The maintainer is on the bypass list of the ruleset, as in the sister project, for a case that cannot wait; the master's own pushes never need it, because GIT-LINEAR refuses a merge commit before GitHub sees it (review: the setting lives on GitHub, not in the repository).

Consequences

  • The integration step of the lead is a rebase and a fast-forward; "Life of a work package" and "The lead's routine" in 04-milestones say so.
  • A rebased package gets new commit IDs. The builder's folder is reset to main for the next package anyway, and a builder whose branch was rebased by the lead does not push the old one again: the new WINn does not follow the master's old WINn, so its first push after the reset needs git push --force-with-lease origin WINn as well.
  • A rebase drops a builder's merge commits, and any conflict resolution inside them; the lead resolves those conflicts again, commit by commit.
  • The selection is wide on purpose (one place, the conservative choice): a merge commit on any local branch that is on no remote blocks a push, also on a stray branch the push does not send. The finding names that branch, so it is rebased or deleted.
  • The WINn branch of a builder may be force-pushed between review rounds, with --force-with-lease, so it can follow main.
  • ADR-0038 (the Merge subject) and ADR-0039 (the checks of the master's push) are amended by this record, and the integration step of ADR-0024 follows it.

Alternatives considered

  • Merge commits (the old flow): keep each package together, but each package appears twice, git bisect walks into the side branches, and the public ruleset would need a bypass. Rejected.
  • Squash each package into one commit: a straight line, but the package's separate commits and their messages are lost. Rejected.

Enforced by

GIT-LINEAR (no merge commit in what a push adds) and GIT-COMMIT-MSG (no merge subject); review for force-pushes and for the ruleset on GitHub.

ADR-0042: The MCP server and how AI apps sign in

Status: Accepted · 2026-11-07 · refines ADR-0013, ADR-0025 (decision 8) and ADR-0029 (decisions 1 and 7); decisions M7-Q3 and M7-Q4

Context

M7 opens Bugaboo to outside AI apps (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, an IDE) through MCP (AI-20 to AI-23). An app acts for a person (ADR-0029, decision 1) and an agent signs in with its own key or through its app (ADR-0029, decision 2). The MCP authorization spec asks for OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and the metadata documents that let an app find the server's sign-in by itself. Architecture §7 planned an authorization server inside Bugaboo with an allow list kept by administrators, but did not say how long a token lives, what happens to a stolen refresh token, which apps may register, what a person sees before an app may act for them, or how a person takes an app's access back. The maintainer accepted the recommendations of M7-Q3 (the consent step and a plain Connected apps list in M7) and M7-Q4 (which apps may register) on 2026-11-07. This record writes it down for WP-05 and WP-09.

Decision

1. One MCP server inside Bugaboo

  • The MCP server is part of the one program (ADR-0001), at /mcp on the server's own port, over the streamable HTTP transport, built with rmcp. It adds no listener and no port (ADR-0023).
  • bb-mcp turns the one tool registry of bb-app into MCP and depends on bb-app only (architecture §4). Every call runs a tool of the registry as the actor, through bb-policy; there is no second rule set (ADR-0013, ADR-0029 decision 1). Enforced by: ARCH-AI-TOOLS, ARCH-DEPS.
  • Answers leave through the same safe types as the API (Authorized<T> with its field mask, PersonRef), so a hidden field never reaches an app (AI-23, M2-F61). Enforced by: ARCH-API-OUT, SEC-MATRIX (the mcp rows).

2. Two ways in: OAuth or an access key

  • OAuth 2.1 (decision 3) is the way for an app a person connects by signing in.
  • An access key is the other way in, for an app that cannot sign in and for agents (Authorization: Bearer bb_…, an agent key for an agent, ADR-0029 decision 2). It counts at /mcp exactly as at /api/v1: the person's evaluation narrowed by the key's choice and projects (ADR-0025, decision 8).
  • A request with neither is answered 401 with the WWW-Authenticate header that names the metadata of decision 3, as the MCP authorization spec asks.

3. The authorization server inside Bugaboo

  • Authorization code with PKCE, the method S256 only (plain is refused). No other grant type: no password grant, no implicit flow, no client credentials.
  • Metadata: the protected-resource metadata (RFC 9728) at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and the authorization-server metadata (RFC 8414) at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, as the MCP authorization spec asks. A token is issued for one resource, the server's /mcp (the resource parameter, RFC 8707), and refused anywhere else, /api/v1 included.
  • Registration (M7-Q4): an app registers itself (dynamic client registration, RFC 7591) when every return address it names is on the person's own computer: http://127.0.0.1 or http://[::1] (a loopback address written as an address, not the name localhost, RFC 8252 §8.3), as Claude Code and Claude Desktop use. The port of a loopback address is not compared, because the app picks a free one at each sign-in (RFC 8252 §7.3). An app whose return address is a web address (https://…) may register only when an administrator added that address under Organization settings › Connections › AI first (Apps that may sign in). Any other address, and a web address not on the list, is refused at registration and again at every sign-in; the return address of a sign-in has to be one the app registered, compared as a whole string (for a loopback address everything but the port). Enforced by: SEC-MATRIX (the OAuth routes) and the tests ai_22_an_app_on_a_web_address_needs_an_administrator_first and ai_22_a_code_without_its_pkce_proof_is_refused (WP-05).
  • Codes and tokens:
    • an authorization code works once and for 60 seconds, and only with its PKCE proof and the return address it was given for; a code used a second time ends the grant it made;
    • an access token lives 15 minutes;
    • a refresh token turns over at each use: the answer carries a new one and the old one is dead. An old refresh token used again ends the whole grant (its access token and every refresh token), because then two parties hold it; the event is in the security log. A refresh token that is not used for 30 days runs out, and a grant ends at the latest after the organization's longest time of an access key (ADR-0025, decision 8), counted from Allow;
    • every code, token and client secret is a random 256-bit secret, stored only as a hash (SHA-256 with a domain of its own, like a session, architecture §7), and never written to a log (DATA-LOGS).
  • Scopes: an app asks for See only or See and change, the words of access keys (ADR-0025, decision 8); Everything I can do and single permissions are not offered to apps. Like a key, a grant may also hold a list of projects, and then counts only in them and their sub-projects. A scope only narrows the person: at every call the grant's permissions are the person's evaluation at that place intersected with the scope, exactly as for an access key, and what no key holds no grant holds (NOT_FOR_KEYS). A grant never reaches the person's own sign-in data. Enforced by: SEC-MATRIX (the mcp rows: a grant with See only, one with See and change), and the property test ai_22_a_grant_can_do_only_what_its_person_can_and_its_scope_allows (WP-05).
  • Who a grant follows: a grant follows its person like a key: a role taken away counts from the next call; while the person is asked for a second step a grant is refused like a key (ADR-0025, decision 7); a person who is switched off or removed loses every grant.

4. The consent step and Connected apps (M7-Q3)

  • The consent step: (on a phone the sentence " wants to work with your account" opens the body, under the bar "Connect an app", because the card heading is for screen readers only there) before a grant is made, the person, signed in in the browser, sees one page: "Claude Code wants to work with your account", what it may do (See only or See and change, the scope it asked for, which the person may narrow to See only), optionally the projects, its return address (on this computer for a loopback address), that the name is the app's own and Bugaboo cannot check it, and that it never does more than the person. Allow makes the grant; Cancel sends the app away with access_denied. The page is asked for every new grant; a remembered consent per app is AI-24 (M12).
  • An agent through its app: an agent signs in with its agent key, or through OAuth when its person allowed that app for the agent: the consent step then names the agent ("Claude Code wants to work as Fixer, agent of Ada Brandt"), and the grant belongs to the agent, narrowed by its work and limits (ADR-0029, decisions 2 and 9).
  • Connected apps (My settings › Sign-in and security): a plain list of the person's grants, each with the app's name, what it may do, when it was allowed and when it was last used, and Take back, which ends the grant at once (its tokens are dead at the next call). The details of each app's use stay in AI-24 (M12).
  • Sign out everywhere ends every grant as it ends access keys (ADR-0025, decision 8), in the same change, each with a security-log entry. A password change leaves grants as it leaves keys. Enforced by: the test ai_22_sign_out_everywhere_ends_every_grant (WP-05).
  • Administrators can switch AI apps off for the organization (a setting under Organization settings › Connections › AI, ADR-0013 amendment M7): no app registers or signs in, and every grant is refused at its next call, but none is deleted, so switching on again brings them back: while AI apps are off, the 30 days without use do not count and oauth.clean-old-grants leaves the grants alone (the longest time still counts). AI switched off for the organization does the same.

5. Runs: a session of an app, an attempt of an agent

  • A session of an app acting for a person (from initialize to its end, or 30 minutes without a call) is one run (ADR-0029, decision 7): its changes are listed together and undone in one step (AI-38), through the port of runs (RunStore, architecture §4).
  • An agent's calls belong to the run of its attempt (ADR-0029, decision 7), whichever MCP session they come in; a session of an agent opens no run of its own.
  • Every event of a call names the person, the channel mcp and the app: the history says "Ada Brandt via Claude Code" (AI-23); an agent's change says "Fixer, agent of Ada Brandt" (ADR-0029, decision 2). Text written through MCP carries Written by an AI app or Written by an agent (COMP-09).

6. Limits and the security log

  • Rate limits per grant and per person (a key counts as its own grant): at most 120 calls a minute for one grant and 240 a minute for one person over all their grants and keys; a call over the limit is answered 429 with the time to wait, and nothing of it is done. Registration and the token endpoint count failed tries per network like sign-in (architecture §7, Limits and abuse). The numbers are named constants of WP-05. Enforced by: the test ai_23_a_grant_over_its_limit_waits_and_changes_nothing (WP-05).
  • The security log has an entry for every registration, every grant made (Allow), every renewal that ends a grant (an old refresh token used again), every Take back, every grant ended by Sign out everywhere, and every refused sign-in of an app (an unknown return address, a code without its proof). A plain renewal of a token is not logged one by one: the grant's last used says it. Enforced by: ARCH-EVENTS.

7. Stored as personal data

Which of these records are personal data, and their marks, are decided once in architecture §12, Personal data in M7. Enforced by: DATA-MARKS.

Consequences

  • New tables for registered apps, grants, codes and refresh tokens, each with its marks; a daily job oauth.clean-old-grants deletes codes and refresh tokens that ran out and grants that were taken back (ADR-0017, amendment M7).
  • New routes outside /api/v1: /mcp, the two metadata documents, registration, the authorization page (the consent step in the browser app) and the token endpoint; SEC-MATRIX gets the entry point mcp.
  • The glossary gains Allow, Take back, Grant (internal) and the app sense of See only and See and change; Connected apps is in M7 in its plain form, and AI-24 keeps what is more.
  • The threats are in architecture §12, Assistant, AI apps and agents (M7).

Amendment (M7, WP-05): what was built

  • No rmcp. Decision 1 named rmcp. The server speaks the few messages MCP needs itself (bb-mcp/src/protocol.rs: initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, resources/templates/list, resources/read, prompts/list, prompts/get; it answers a request in its own JSON response and never opens a stream, so GET is 405). The newest version of rmcp follows a protocol that has no session and brings its own rules for hosts and origins; the token, the scope, the run and the limits are Bugaboo's own, and each request carries its token, so the library would only have carried the JSON. The server answers with the version the app asks for when it knows it (2025-11-25 down to 2024-11-05) and otherwise with its newest. A different decision is open again when the protocol settles (M7-F40). Nothing else in this record changes.
  • Where the sign-in lives. The routes apps call stand outside /api/v1 and answer in the words of OAuth: GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource, GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, POST /oauth/register and POST /oauth/token. The consent step is the page /connect of the browser app, which asks GET and POST /api/v1/oauth/authorization; Connected apps is GET /api/v1/oauth/apps and DELETE /api/v1/oauth/apps/{app}; the web addresses an administrator allows are below /api/v1/oauth/web-addresses. A token of an app opens nothing outside /mcp, also not in a cookie.
  • Secrets. A code, an access token and a renewing token are 256 random bits written with the starts bbc_, bba_ and bbr_ (an access key starts bb_), each in a hash domain of its own. The swap of a code or a renewing token uses the secret up in the same change that writes the new tokens, so two requests with one secret cannot both succeed.
  • One narrowing. narrowing_for turns See only or See and change (the words of access keys) and the projects into the narrowing of the policy engine, for a key and for a grant alike. Ctx::actor is the one way from a token to an actor: a cookie, an access key (bb_) or the token of an app (bba_).
  • The switch of AI apps is the setting ai-apps.enabled (on at the start; since WP-15 it does not depend on the switch of the assistant, and a project can switch AI apps off for itself, see ADR-0013, amendment WP-15). While it is off, registration, sign-in and every call are refused as for any token that does not work; no grant is deleted.
  • Runs and the app on the event. A session is one run per grant (or key): the first call starts the run (initialize too), the calls that follow within 30 minutes go on in it, a call after 30 minutes without one starts another, and a sweeper closes the idle ones. The app's name is kept with the run (change_run.app), and an event of the run names the run, so the history reads it from there: HistoryItem::app. An event carries no column of its own for the app.
  • Limits. 120 calls a minute for a grant (a key counts as its own grant) and 240 for a person, in the one fixed window of the rest of the server (bb_app::rate_window). Every message to /mcp counts, counted once at the entry (mcp_identity); a call over the limit gets 429 with the time to wait and does nothing, and a tool call gets a result with isError and the sentence of the limit with the wait. The security log has an entry for it (ai_call.limited). A network may register 20 apps an hour; a registration is written to the security log and not to the history, because it has no person.
  • The entry of MCP. One request holds one message: a batch is refused. Where the public address of the server is not set, the sign-in tells apps the address the request came to and the server says so in its log when it starts; a server that apps reach from the internet needs its public address. A page of another website is turned away: its Origin has to be the one the request came to (the rule of the API) and the public address of the server where it is known, which also stops a name pointed at the machine (DNS rebinding). AI apps switched off turn away every credential at the entry, access keys and agent keys too, and that is no guess of a network. A session secret does not open /mcp. bb-mcp reads a request through bb-api (the client, the origin, the token, the answers in the words of another protocol), written once there.
  • Pausing while apps are off. The daily clean-up deletes nothing while apps are off and moves the end of every renewing token that was not used by the time since the last pause (the first pause only marks the moment, and the clean-up that runs with apps on clears the mark), so the days without use do not count. A grant past its end (the longest time) is not listed and not counted, and the clean-up deletes it 30 days later.

Alternatives considered

  • An outside authorization server (an identity provider of the customer): the MCP spec allows it, but a self-hosted Bugaboo would then need one to run, and the scopes would live in two places. Rejected for M7; company sign-in (OIDC) can sign the person in on the consent page.
  • Open registration for every return address: any web page could register as "Claude" and collect grants through a link. Rejected (M7-Q4): web addresses need an administrator.
  • Only access keys, no OAuth: a person would copy a long secret into every app, and the MCP apps expect OAuth. Rejected; keys stay as the second way.
  • Long access tokens without refresh: a stolen token would work for days. Rejected; 15 minutes and rotation make a theft short and visible.
  • A remembered consent per app in M7: more screens and rules than M7 needs. Moved to AI-24 (M12, M7-Q3).

Enforced by

SEC-MATRIX (the mcp rows), ARCH-API-OUT, ARCH-AI-TOOLS, ARCH-DEPS, ARCH-EVENTS, DATA-MARKS, DATA-LOGS (see tools/checks/catalog.toml), and the tests named above and in WP-05.

Amendment (M9, secure defaults): ai apps start off

  • AI apps start off (ai-apps.enabled, ADR-0047 decision 6 and its amendment): every kind of AI is off in a new installation until an administrator switches it on. This replaces the on at the start of this record.
  • An upgrade keeps them as they were. A stored value is only a change of the default, so migration 59 writes on as the organization's own value where a person already exists and the organization set no value of its own; a value the organization set stays. Enforced by: the tests of migration 59 on both databases, comp_04_every_setting_that_matters_for_security_starts_safe.

ADR-0043: Dates and dependencies

Status: Accepted · 2026-11-11 · refines PLAN-01, PLAN-02, PLAN-03, PLAN-04 and ADR-0030; the maintainer's answers M8-Q1, M8-Q2 and M8-Q3

Context

The timeline draws issues as bars over days, so an issue needs dates. Before M8 an issue has Estimated time and Time left, but no start date, and Due date is only a field key that search cannot read and forms block (M3-F101). Own fields can be dates. PLAN-01 asks that the dates come from start and due fields, "configurable which ones".

Relations are rows of kinds that the organization edits (blocks, duplicate of, causes, related to). None of them means anything for dates, although blocks says what the glossary calls Must finish first. PLAN-02 asks for that dependency in M8 and for start together, finish together and finish when it starts in V1, and it asks for one relation model for issues, the timeline and the map.

Many planning tools push the issues that wait when an earlier one moves. ADR-0030 rejected bars that move by themselves: it surprises people and breaks dates someone promised.

The exit demo of M8 asks for "a warning for the release", but releases (ISS-08) come in M10.

Decision

  1. Two built-in date fields, Start date and Due date (M8-Q1). Both are fields of the field catalogue in bb-core, like Estimated time: a calendar date with no time of day and no time zone, stored on the issue (migration 49).
